ARC01.blurb:
This is the opening ranking round of the archery program, and it is not ticketed. Women's compound and men's recurve archers each shoot to set their seeding.

The women's compound round is the first ever at the Games. It seeds the debut compound mixed team event, so every arrow shapes who meets whom on July 21.

Because it is not ticketed, treat it as a preview of the brackets to come. Ticketed head-to-head action at Carson Stadium starts later in the week.

potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist and world No. 2 as of September 2026. He would be competing at a home Games if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Alexis Ruiz

potentialContenders.name: Chikitha Taniparthi

ARC02.blurb:
Day two of ranking rounds, again not ticketed, covers men's compound and women's recurve. These scores decide the seeds for the compound mixed team bracket and the women's individual recurve bracket.

Men's compound is new to the Games. The round also sets up the first compound medal event, which begins the following evening.

The women's recurve field is wide open for 2028, with Korea's dominance tested by archers from China, Czechia and India.

potentialContenders.name: Marie Horackova

ARC03.blurb:
Compound archery gets its first medal here. The compound mixed team event runs from the 1/8 round to the gold medal match in one evening, and it is the first archery medal event of the 2028 Games.

Twelve teams of one man and one woman compete. Compound bows have pulleys, magnifying sights and release aids, so expect tight scoring and a lot of perfect tens.

India is the storyline to watch. It has never won an archery medal at the Games, and its compound archers hope this event delivers the first.

Carson Stadium seats about 27,000 for archery, and every seat sits close to the field. The evening session should feel like a debut night.

ARC04.blurb:
Recurve individual eliminations begin with the 1/32 round, where the field of up to 64 archers per gender is cut in half. Top seeds face low seeds, but one cold end can still end a campaign.

Matches are best-of-five sets, three arrows per set. Early rounds are a good way to see many nations and a few big names at close range.

The morning session at Carson Stadium suits a first visit. The stadium is a soccer venue with clear sight lines, converted for archery.

ARC05.blurb:
An evening of recurve eliminations at Carson Stadium covers the end of the 1/32 round and the start of the 1/16 round. Men's and women's matches run side by side, so there is always a target to watch.

The shoot-off, one arrow each closest to the center, can end a match without warning. Early rounds are where upsets tend to appear.

The stadium hosted the 2003 FIFA Women's World Cup final, and rugby sevens plays there the week before archery. Under evening light, this should be an easy session to settle into.

ARC06.blurb:
The first Sunday morning session continues the recurve individual 1/32 and 1/16 rounds for men and women. It is a long, steady block of head-to-head archery with the field narrowing.

Korea won all five recurve golds in Paris, but its 2028 women's lineup looks different. Im Si-hyeon, a triple gold medalist, finished 10th at the 2026 national trials and missed that year's team.

A morning at Carson Stadium is a relaxed way to catch the bracket as it takes shape.

ARC07.blurb:
Sunday evening brings more 1/32 and 1/16 matches under the lights. With hundreds of arrows flying, it is a good window on how the top seeds handle pressure.

Brady Ellison, the Paris silver medalist, would be on home soil in 2028 if he is selected. A US crowd at a Los Angeles-area stadium could make his early matches a highlight.

The seating at Carson Stadium keeps fans close to the line, so you can hear the shots and the crowd's reaction.

This is a dedicated women's recurve session, covering the 1/32 and 1/16 rounds. The field is thinning toward the knockout stage, and the favorites are less clear than in past cycles.

Im Si-hyeon won in Paris, but the 2026 results show a wider field. Kang Chaeyoung, Zhu Jingyi and Marie Horackova all won major 2026 events, and India's Kumkum Mohod has made a name at 17.

A mid-morning session at Carson Stadium is a quiet way to watch the bracket.

ARC09.blurb:
Men's recurve team medals are decided in one evening. Three-archer teams shoot from the quarterfinals through the bronze and gold matches.

Korea won gold in Paris, with France silver and Türkiye bronze. Korea's trio went on to win the 2025 world title, then three straight 2026 World Cup team events.

The USA took silver at the 2025 worlds, and India lost 5-1 to Korea in the 2026 Asian Games final. Expect a real contest for the podium.

Carson Stadium should be loud for a medal night, with team matches that move quickly. Arrive early for the quarterfinals.

A mid-morning session focuses entirely on men's individual recurve, with the 1/32 and 1/16 rounds. It is an easy way to see a full range of nations before the knockout matches get tighter.

Recent winners are spread across Asia and Europe. Dhiraj Bommadevara won the 2026 World Cup Final, and Lee Woo-seok won the 2026 Asian Games title.

Carson Stadium is open-air, so expect a bright, relaxed atmosphere on the field.

ARC11.blurb:
Women's recurve team medals are decided in a single evening, starting at the quarterfinals. Three archers per team shoot in set-play matches through bronze and gold.

Korea won gold in Paris, but its streak is under pressure. India beat Korea 5-3 at the 2026 Asian Games, ending Korea's run of seven straight Asian Games titles.

Chinese Taipei won the 2025 world title, and the USA reached the 2026 Madrid World Cup final. The field looks open.

A medal night at Carson Stadium should draw a big crowd, and the team format brings frequent roars.

ARC12.blurb:
The recurve mixed team 1/8 round opens the bracket. One man and one woman from the same nation shoot together, and seeding comes from the ranking rounds.

Korea won in Paris, with Germany silver and the USA bronze. Since then, Spain's pairing has taken over, winning the 2025 world title and the Madrid 2026 World Cup stage.

Pairs shoot quickly, so matches run fast at Carson Stadium. This is a good session for a first look at the format.

Recurve mixed team medals are decided in an evening session, from the quarterfinals through the bronze and gold matches. Pairs shoot against the clock, and a single miss can swing a match.

Korea has won this event at Paris 2024, but Spain has become the team to beat. Elia Canales and Andres Temino beat Korea in the 2025 world final and won at Madrid 2026.

Seeing the medal matches at Carson Stadium means a loud, close-quarters finish. Expect lead changes late.

Brady Ellison would be at a home Games if selected, and Andres Temino arrives as the 2025 world champion. Korea's Lee Woo-seok and India's Dhiraj Bommadevara both won big events in 2026.

Carson Stadium is a good spot to watch the knockout round start in earnest.

ARC15.blurb:
The men's individual recurve medals are decided here, from the quarterfinals through the bronze and gold matches. It is the last big individual night of the archery program.

Kim Woojin beat Brady Ellison in a shoot-off for gold in Paris. A rematch is possible in 2028, though neither is confirmed, and Andres Temino arrives as the reigning world champion.

Shoot-offs can settle gold in one arrow, so the final seats at Carson Stadium may be the tensest in the sport.

Sixteen archers remain at the 1/8 elimination round, and the bracket starts to bite. One bad end can end a medal run, and the final day of the archery program has begun.

The women's recurve field is wide open. Paris 2024 gold medalist Im Si-hyeon missed Korea's 2026 national team, so Korea's 2028 lineup is not settled. Kang Chaeyoung, Zhu Jingyi and Marie Horackova are the names shaping the field.

This is a morning session at Carson Stadium, a soccer-specific venue where every seat sits close to the action. Expect a quieter, more intimate crowd than the evening finals, with plenty of matches to follow.

ARC17.blurb:
The last medal session of the archery program, and the women's individual recurve gold is the final archery title of the 2028 Games. Quarterfinals, semifinals and both medal matches fit into one evening.

Korea won this event in Paris 2024, when Im Si-hyeon beat teammate Nam Su-hyeon in an all-Korean final and Lisa Barbelin of France took bronze. Im missed Korea's 2026 national team, so the field is open.

Reigning world champion Kang Chaeyoung is a projected favorite, if she qualifies. Zhu Jingyi of China and Czechia's Marie Horackova have both shown strong recent form, and Horackova beat Valencia 6-0 in the 2026 World Cup Final.

The session is at Carson Stadium, which will seat 27,000 for archery and hosted the 2003 FIFA Women's World Cup final. Expect a big night-time crowd and a shoot-off or two.

ATH01.blurb:
Track and field opens at the Coliseum with a morning that carries a lot of events. The women's and men's 100m begin here with preliminary rounds and Round 1, and the women's 100m will finish with its final that same evening.

Field athletes qualify for the women's shot put and hammer and the men's pole vault. The women's 5000m and 800m also run their first rounds, so this session helps set the evening's final fields.

The Coliseum is an open bowl with no roof, so expect Southern California sun and a crowd still filling in. It's a relaxed way to see the stadium and a wide range of events before the medals start.

ATH02.blurb:
Day one ends with a sprint final. The women's 100m semifinal and final fall in the same evening session, the first time the event has opened the athletics program at the Games.

Two more medals are awarded here, in the women's shot put and the men's 10,000m. Men's 400m hurdles and women's triple jump rounds also run in the field and track program.

The open-air bowl should be at its fullest and loudest for the first night. Sit near the finish line for the 100m, or toward the shot put circle if you want to watch a throwing final up close.

ATH03.blurb:
Day two begins with a morning that mixes the first events of the decathlon with multiple qualifying rounds. The men's decathlon starts with the 100m, long jump and shot put.

Qualifying also runs for the women's discus, men's shot put and men's long jump. The mixed 4x400m relay has its first round, and the women's 800m repechage is the second chance for runners who missed automatic advancement.

This is a good value session for fans who like watching field events up close. The men's 100m final comes later in the day, but the early crowd tends to be there for the specialists.

ATH04.blurb:
The men's 100m final is the big event of day two. The semifinals and final run back to back, so the Coliseum will see who becomes the fastest man in the Games.

Three more medals are decided: the men's shot put, the women's hammer and the mixed 4x400m relay. The decathlon continues with the high jump and 400m, and the men's 1500m opens with Round 1.

Expect a full stadium and a packed schedule. Night sessions at the Coliseum should have electricity at the 100m start, so the semis are worth catching as well.

ATH05.blurb:
One medal is on the line this morning, in the women's triple jump. It is a good session for fans who like a single event with a live final.

The rest is early rounds. The men's 400m and women's 3000m steeplechase have Round 1, the 400m hurdles repechage gives eliminated runners a second chance, and the decathlon continues with the 110m hurdles, discus and pole vault.

The triple jump runway is a fun place to watch from. Expect the crowd to clap along with the jumpers as the sun climbs over the open bowl.

The Coliseum should feel very different after dark. The relay debut will be a first for the Games, so even casual fans could enjoy seeing it live.

Round 1 runs in the men's 3000m steeplechase, women's 400m and men's 110m hurdles. The hurdlers are fun to watch up close, and the steeplechase has a barrier and a water jump in front of the crowd.

Pole vault qualifying should have a good rhythm, with the bar rising and athletes entering gradually. The morning crowd tends to be fans who love details.

Expect a loud crowd as the 800m runners come around the final bend. The high jump bar and the discus cage give the infield action all night.

Qualifying runs for the men's hammer and women's long jump. The 400m repechage for men and women and the men's 200m repechage are second-chance rounds under the 2028 format.

The session is worth it for variety and a lighter crowd. Long jump qualifying has a steady rhythm of runners and sand.

The women's discus and men's long jump finals are also on the card. Round 1 of the women's 1500m and 200m and the men's 110m hurdles repechage run too.

Expect a full house for the 1500m, when the bell rings. The hurdles bring a different thrill, with the runners rushing through the final straight.

The men's 3000m steeplechase final is the only medal event this morning. It is a good test of tactics, with barriers and water jumps adding drama to every lap.

Qualifying also runs for the women's javelin and high jump. Men's 800m Round 1 and the women's 200m repechage give a look at fast runners trying to advance.

This is a laid-back session. Fans who like field events can get close to the javelin and high jump action.

Semifinals in the men's and women's 400m, men's 110m hurdles and men's 200m are also on the card. Those rounds show who is peaking early.

The pole vault crowd is often among the loudest, clapping the athletes into each attempt. The hurdles bring a loud finish, when runners clear the last barrier.

Round 1 runs in the men's 5000m and women's 100m hurdles, and the men's 800m repechage gives another chance to advance. It is a day for fans who like to see a bit of everything.

The triple jump's hop, step and jump make it great for the crowd. The heptathlon is easy to follow, with points building over two days.

ATH16.blurb:
Sunday afternoon at the Coliseum is a stack of medal finals. The men's 800m, women's 1500m, women's high jump, women's javelin and men's 4x100m relay all award medals in under three hours.

The 800m is the headliner. Emmanuel Wanyonyi, the Paris 2024 champion, won the 2025 world title in 1:41.86, with Djamel Sedjati and Marco Arop within a tenth of a second. If that trio qualifies, the final could be tight.

Relay heats and the women's 100m hurdles semifinals fill the gaps. In the women's 1500m, Faith Kipyegon is expected back in 2027 after missing time in 2026, so her 2028 form is an open question.

The Coliseum is an open-air bowl, so expect afternoon sun and field events running alongside the track. The crowd can switch between a high jump bar and a sprint relay finish without leaving their seats.

The final stadium session at the Coliseum goes out with six medal finals in under two hours. The men's 5000m, women's 100m hurdles, both 4x400m relays, the women's 4x100m and the men's javelin all award medals.

In the 5000m, Jakob Ingebrigtsen returned from February 2026 Achilles surgery and beat Cole Hocker at the 2026 Ultimate Championship, 12:59.24 to 13:00.05. Hocker is the reigning world champion. If both are healthy in 2028, expect a tactical race.

The relays could add drama. The US women won the 2025 world 4x400m with Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone, who took 2026 off to have her daughter, and Botswana's men won the world 4x400m.

This is the last night of track at the 1932 and 1984 Games venue, and the stadium should feel like it. Road events follow from July 27.

ATH18.blurb:
Two medal races, one morning. The men's and women's half-marathon race walk finals share a single session on Thursday, July 27, with the new 21.1 km distance replacing the 20 km walks.

There are no heats, so each race is a straight final. The order of the two races had not been announced when the schedule came out, so check before you plan your arrival.

The event is also a changing of the guard. The mixed marathon walk relay from Paris 2024 has been dropped, and walkers such as Canada's Evan Dunfee have criticized that choice.

The venue and course are still unannounced. Race walks are usually staged on a looped road circuit, so spectators can often see the field pass several times as the pack stretches out.

ATH19.blurb:
The women's marathon is a single-race final with no heats. It starts at 7:15 AM on the Venice Beach Boardwalk, with the Pacific on one side and the boardwalk scene on the other.

Paris 2024 produced a Games record of 2:22:55 from Sifan Hassan, who beat Tigst Assefa in a sprint finish. The field has changed fast since then, and the sport's depth has grown sharply.

Fans would watch the start from the roadside rather than from stadium seats. The finish area and full route have not been announced, so check the route before planning your day.

The men's marathon is the last athletics event of the 2028 Games. It is a single-race final starting at 7:15 AM at the Venice Beach Boardwalk, on the closing Sunday of the track and field program.

The sport has moved quickly since Paris 2024, where Tamirat Tola set a Games record of 2:06:26. In 2026, Sabastian Sawe ran 1:59:30 in London, the first sub-two-hour marathon in a race. Course conditions will differ in Los Angeles, so Games-record talk is speculative.

Fans would watch the start from the roadside, with the beach, palm trees and Venice street scene behind them. The finish area has not been announced.

BDM01.blurb:
The first morning of badminton at the 2028 Games is group play across all the doubles events and both singles draws, and it is a good way to see the whole field at once.

The men's singles title will change hands, since Viktor Axelsen has retired. That leaves an open draw, with 2026 world champion Alex Lanier of France among those projected to lead it.

Galen Center is a compact, two-deck arena of about 10,000 seats, so even upper-level seats sit fairly close to the courts. It is next to the Jefferson/USC Metro station on the USC campus.

Doubles take center stage in this afternoon group session, with women's singles alongside. Each doubles event has only 16 pairs, so every group match carries weight.

None of the Paris 2024 mixed or women's gold medalists are expected back as pairs. Zheng Siwei and Huang Yaqiong have retired, as has Chen Qingchen, so new champions are certain.

The 4.5-hour window is short enough for a relaxed afternoon visit. Expect the arena to be only partly full, which makes it easy to get close to the action.

Men's doubles has no defending pair. Paris 2024 gold medalist Lee Yang has retired, which leaves Chinese Taipei without its title-winning partnership and the field more open.

Evening sessions tend to feel livelier than the morning ones, with the arena under the lights and the crowd building as matches run late. Galen Center's modest size keeps the noise close to the courts.

The men's singles field is wide open with Axelsen retired. France is a storyline, with Christo Popov winning the 2025 World Tour Finals and Alex Lanier the 2026 world title.

Early sessions in a group stage are an easy way into the sport. The matches are fast, the tickets are typically the more accessible ones, and you can walk to the arena from the Jefferson/USC station.

Each doubles event needs at least one pair from each of the five continental confederations, so the draw includes pairs from places that rarely reach the final. Canada's Victor Lai is one such story, having won back-to-back world bronze medals.

A short afternoon block is a good fit for a first-timer. You can see a lot of rallies in a few hours.

Lee Yang's retirement ended the Paris 2024 gold-medal pair. Liang Weikeng and Wang Chang lost that final in three games and then won the 2026 world title.

Night sessions bring a loud, packed feel to the 10,000-seat bowl. It is a good choice if you want to see the most players in a single ticket.

BWF says the shorter format aims for more competitive matches and more consistent lengths. That could mean faster turnaround and more matches per session.

The morning slot is a good time to see the top players while the crowds are smaller. Galen Center's close seating keeps the rallies in clear view.

Japan's Kodai Naraoka reached the 2026 world final as the 10th seed. Chinese Taipei's Chou Tien-chen took bronze as sixth seed.

A midday session at Galen Center is a relaxed way to see a mix of events. It is easy to reach by Metro and has plenty of room around the concourse.

Tuesday morning is group play in both doubles events and both singles events. It is a quieter slot, with no mixed doubles.

It is a good chance to watch players like 2026 world champion Alex Lanier early, before the field narrows.

Korea's Baek Ha-na and Lee So-hee beat China's Liu Shengshu and Tan Ning in the 2026 world final. This session is a good look at that rivalry.

The quarterfinals are the first elimination matches in the event. Expect a louder crowd at Galen Center as the stakes rise.

Men's singles has no Axelsen after his retirement in April 2026. Alex Lanier and Christo Popov give France two serious names, and Canada's Victor Lai is a rising story.

An Se-young won 11 titles in 2025 and then the 2026 world title without dropping a game. It will be telling to see how the women's field responds.

Wednesday night closes group play in men's and women's singles before the round of 16. It is the last chance for players to book a knockout spot.

The scoring is expected to be best of three games to 15 points, under a BWF change effective January 2027, though no Games-specific confirmation was found. That would make every point count.

A late singles session is a good choice if you want to see the draw take shape. The arena's compact layout keeps you close to the court.

Three events share one long morning at the Galen Center. Mixed doubles semifinals, women's doubles quarterfinals and women's singles round-of-16 matches put the sport's variety on display.

The mixed doubles title is guaranteed a new owner: Paris 2024 champions Zheng Siwei and Huang Yaqiong retired in December 2025. The women's doubles field is also reshuffled, since Chen Qingchen retired and split her pair with Jia Yifan.

The arena holds roughly 10,000 on two decks, so even upper seats sit close to the court. An early start suits fans who want several matches in a single sitting.

Men's singles is wide open. Viktor Axelsen retired in April 2026 because of chronic back problems, so a new champion will be crowned. France's Alex Lanier won the 2026 world title, and Shi Yuqi's fitness is a question mark.

The women's side carries more continuity, with An Se-young a projected favorite. Afternoon sessions in the compact Galen Center keep fans near the court, so you can see the rallies up close.

The recent world titlists are Korea and China, which makes for a stacked quarterfinal slate. At night the Galen Center crowd is loud, and fast net exchanges echo through the arena.

The arena seats about 10,200, close enough to the floor that you can hear every shuttle strike and the doubles rallies feel fast and loud.

Host USA is already in both fields. The USA women won the 2026 World Cup, and Latvia's men are the reigning World Cup champions.

Latvia won the 2026 World Cup, with Karlis Lasmanis as MVP and top scorer. Serbia took bronze, France finished fourth, and Spain won the 2025 title.

Valley Complex 3 is one of four temporary complexes in the Sepulveda Basin's Valley Zone. Expect a lively crowd as the afternoon cools into evening.

The women's field is wide open. The USA won the 2026 World Cup, the Netherlands won in 2025, and Canada beat the USA in the 2026 AmeriCup final.

At Paris 2024, the top two pool finishers went straight to the semifinals, with places three through six in play-in games. The 12-team format at 2028 adds more teams and games.

The 9 p.m. start puts the temporary octagon under lights at the end of a long pool stage. Expect tight games and a vocal crowd.

Four games, two genders, and one brand-new wrinkle: a play-in round that exists because the field grew from 8 to 12 teams per gender. Expect high-stakes, short-fuse basketball with quarterfinal spots on the line.

At Paris 2024, teams placed third to sixth in pool play contested play-ins. The 2028 format adds quarterfinals, so exactly who lands here is still to be determined.

Valley Complex 3 is a temporary eight-sided stand around a single court in the Sepulveda Basin, so fans watch from every side. This afternoon slot is a relaxed way to see 3x3 up close.

Netherlands and Germany arrive as defending men's and women's champions if they qualify. Latvia's men won both the 2026 World Cup and Europe Cup, while the USA women won the 2026 World Cup.

The early-evening session at the Sepulveda Basin's temporary arena should feel loud and close, with fans on all eight sides of the single court.

The field is full of Paris 2024 storylines. Lithuania took men's bronze, and Spain, the women's silver medalists, won the 2024 Europe Cup title afterward.

With a 9 p.m. tip and fans on every side of the court, this should be one of the livelier atmospheres of the 3x3 week.

Two men's and two women's semifinals are the last step before the medal games, with a gold-medal game on the line and a bronze game as the consolation. The finalists will be set, then play again later the same night.

The Paris 2024 semifinals gave us Latvia's upset loss to France after a perfect pool run. The Netherlands later beat France 18-17 in overtime for gold.

Expect close, physical games in the temporary Sepulveda Basin arena, and a full crowd that will stay for the medal games after dark.

Under the lights in the Sepulveda Basin, with every seat close to the single court, expect a loud, tense finale.

Basketball tips off at the 2028 Games with a two-game women's doubleheader, two days before the Opening Ceremony. You'd be in the building for the first basketball of the entire tournament.

Two group-phase games run from noon to about 4:15 PM at Intuit Dome. The hosts are chasing a ninth straight title after the 67-66 escape against France at Paris 2024, though the matchups are not yet set.

Intuit Dome opened in 2024 and holds about 18,000. Look for The Wall, 51 rows of steep seats behind one basket, under a huge halo video board.

The men's tournament opens on Thursday with two games in one session, the day before the Opening Ceremony. It's a full afternoon of group-phase basketball.

The USA qualifies as host and is chasing a sixth straight title after beating France 98-87 in Paris 2024. Kevin Durant has said he plans to play in 2028, while LeBron James has said he won't and Stephen Curry has called a return unlikely.

Intuit Dome is built for noise, with The Wall, a 51-row block of seats behind one basket. A two-game session gives you time to settle in and watch how the tournament shapes up.

An 8 PM Monday game at Intuit Dome should be one of the loudest sessions of the week.

The USA owns eight straight gold medals, and its 2026 World Cup roster was the second-youngest it has sent to that event. Spain won bronze there, a sign of how deep the field is.

The late slot suits Intuit Dome. The Wall fans bring loud energy, and the halo board gives the arena a big-event feel.

BMF01.blurb:
Twenty-four riders are in the 2028 Games BMX Freestyle park field, 12 men and 12 women, and this morning session is where the qualification round for both events plays out on one course. It is the first look at the park.

Riders get timed, 60-second runs to show difficulty, execution and creativity. The format has not changed from Paris 2024, so expect big tricks early as riders chase a spot in the next day's final.

Qualification points run through World Championships, World Cups and the May-June 2028 Q-Series, so the exact field is still unsettled. Recent form points to strong Japanese, Chinese, British and American riders.

Valley Complex 1 is a temporary open-air venue in the Sepulveda Basin, near the 405 and 101 freeways. A 10:30 AM start means a relaxed morning with a close view of the riders, in the sport's home region.

Gold medals in men's and women's park are decided in this one session. Each final has up to 12 riders, and the Paris 2024 podiums were among the tightest the sport has produced.

As in Paris, each rider is expected to get two 60-second runs, with only the better score counting. One clean run can win it. In Paris, Torres Gil took the men's title with his first run, and Deng Yawen led the women's final.

The field is still open. None of the Paris 2024 medalists in either event had confirmed or ruled out 2028 in the sources reviewed, so nothing here is certain.

Expect a lively atmosphere at Valley Complex 1 in the Sepulveda Basin, in the sport's California heartland. A late-morning start suits a sunny, festival-style crowd.

BMX racing opens in the Sepulveda Basin with men's and women's quarterfinals and last chance runs. Riders race for places in the next day's semifinals.

The heats are short, fast and unforgiving. One clipped jump or tangled first turn can end a run, and last chance runs give a stumbling rider one more shot.

The temporary course is set into the basin's natural terrain, ringed by open fields and golf courses. Expect full summer sun at 10:30 AM. Fans can ride the Metro G Line to Woodley Station.

Medal day for BMX racing. Men's and women's semifinals and finals are decided in one morning session, and two champions leave the dirt with gold.

France swept the men's podium at Paris 2024, and Australia's Saya Sakakibara won the women's title. Whether those stars return in 2028 is unconfirmed, and the sport's current form points to a wide-open field.

The San Fernando Valley hosts Games competition for the first time here. BMX has local roots too: the first organized BMX race was held at Palms Park in West Los Angeles in 1969.

Single elimination means one loss ends a tournament. Early bouts often pit seeded veterans against first-time qualifiers, so upsets are part of the draw.

The theater is better known for award shows than for fights. Expect a raised ring on the big stage, tiered seats facing it, air conditioning, and L.A. Live buzzing right outside.

The game is a Friday night affair at OKC Softball Park, the ballpark known as the "Mecca of Softball." Expect a loud, close-to-the-field atmosphere and cooler air than the daytime heat.

CER01A.blurb:
For the first time in modern Games history, the Opening Ceremony will play out across two stadiums at once. The 2028 Stadium in Inglewood and the LA Memorial Coliseum will share the same Friday evening kickoff.

Film producer Kathleen Kennedy, former Lucasfilm president, is Head of Ceremonies and Content, working alongside Ben Winston and Scott Givens. Openings traditionally feature an athlete parade, an artistic program and the cauldron lighting, though show details remain under wraps.

The Inglewood venue is sunk into the ground beneath a translucent canopy, with open sides that let in the coastal breeze and a ring-shaped video board overhead. Top seats have reportedly sold for more than $5,000, so this is a premium ticket.

The schedule puts the first medals of the Games, in women's triathlon, right after the ceremony.

CER02.blurb:
The Games close on Sunday evening, July 30, with a farewell staged entirely at the LA Memorial Coliseum. Plans originally split the show with Inglewood, but the Los Angeles City Council voted unanimously in November 2025 to keep it at the Coliseum.

Closing ceremonies typically bring a mix of athletes, music and spectacle, capped by the flag handover to the next host city. Kathleen Kennedy, as Head of Ceremonies and Content, is shaping the farewell, though specific programming hasn't been announced.

Paris 2024 set a high bar for the handover, with Tom Cruise arriving from the stadium roof and a pre-recorded Los Angeles segment featuring Billie Eilish, Snoop Dogg and the Red Hot Chili Peppers.

The Coliseum is an open-air bowl dating to 1923, entered through the arched Peristyle plaza beneath the cauldron tower. It is expected to become the first venue to host events at three Summer Games, so this send-off carries real historical weight.

The format is T20, a fast, roughly three-hour contest, and six women's teams are chasing gold, silver and bronze. Most matchdays are morning and evening double-headers, so this 9:00 AM start opens a full day of cricket.

The Fairgrounds Cricket Stadium sits inside the Pomona fairgrounds, about 30 miles east of downtown LA, with roughly 10,000 seats close to the boundary. Expect an early sun-soaked, first-day buzz.

CKT23.blurb:
Day two of the second round gives early risers another morning of T20 cricket in Pomona. The format is fast, with each side batting twenty overs, so a full match fits inside the session.

It is a group-stage match, so net run rate and every close finish could matter. The final matchups depend on qualifiers set for January and February 2028.

The temporary-feeling Fairplex setting is part of the draw. The Los Angeles County Fair has been held here since 1922, and now it hosts a sport making its first Games return in 128 years.
CKT23.potentialContendersIntro: The final matchups are unknown. These are projected teams, with the sixth place still to be decided in qualifying.

potentialContenders.name: India
potentialContenders.note: Reigning T20 World Cup champions from 2026. Under new captain Shreyas Iyer, their form is a storyline to watch.

potentialContenders.name: Australia
potentialContenders.note: Projected Oceania qualifier, if the rankings hold through the 2026 cutoff.

potentialContenders.name: South Africa
potentialContenders.note: Projected to hold the Africa place based on November 2026 rankings.

CKT24.blurb:
This evening match on Wednesday could carry real weight as the group stage heads toward its close. A loss here may leave a team with little room to recover.

The field is still taking shape. Four continental places are projected, the United States is the host, and one team will emerge from the eight-team qualifier in early 2028.

Evening cricket at Fairplex suits the format. Floodlights, a close-in crowd of about 10,000 and a quick three-hour match make it an easy first cricket outing.

potentialContenders.name: United States

CKT25.blurb:
Thursday morning brings the last scheduled men's group-stage play before the medal matches. Any result here could separate a team heading to bronze or gold from one going home.

With so few matches left, every over matters. The qualifier winner is still unknown, and so are the final standings.

The Pomona fairgrounds setting makes a morning match feel like a county-fair day with international cricket. Seats sit close to the boundary under inland Southern California sun, so bring sunscreen.

potentialContenders.name: South Africa

CKT26.blurb:
The final night of men's group play could have a knockout feel. It is the last chance for teams to set up the bronze and gold matches on July 28 and 29.

Because the qualifier is not until early 2028, the exact field is still unknown. Scenarios could come down to a single over or a tight run rate.

Pomona's evening crowd should be at full volume, with about 10,000 fans near the boundary. The match is a fair-grounds night out with real stakes.
CKT26.potentialContendersIntro: No pairing is confirmed. These teams are projected from 2026 results, pending the January-February 2028 qualifiers.

CKT27.blurb:
Bronze is not a consolation prize in a sport waiting 128 years for its return. This morning match on July 28 decides the men's third-place medal.

The teams are unknown, since both semi-final-style routes depend on group results. The six-team field limits how many sides have a shot at this match.

The Fairgrounds stadium offers a close, open-air setting for a medal match. Expect an early-morning crowd with national flags and a big day on the line.

CKT28.blurb:
The gold medal match closes the cricket program and brings the sport's first Games final since Great Britain beat France in Paris in 1900. It is a historic morning in Pomona.

India are the reigning T20 World Cup champions after beating New Zealand by 96 runs in 2026. England overtook India at No. 1 that July, so a Great Britain-India final is a plausible storyline, not a certainty.

Expect a sold-out ground of about 10,000, packed close to the boundary. The setting is a temporary-feeling Fairplex stadium, with a final that could define the sport's Games comeback.

potentialContenders.name: Suryakumar Yadav
potentialContenders.note: Named Games gold as his next goal after the 2026 final, but was dropped from the T20I side. A comeback is speculative.

CLB01.blurb:
Climbing opens with a morning semifinal on the Pacific shore. Boulder has never had a standalone medal at the Games, so every top finish here carries new weight.

The field plays out on short, punishing problems where one slip can cost a spot in the final. Japan's Sorato Anraku, the 2025 world champion, is the reference point after a dominant 2026 season. His 2028 spot is not yet confirmed.

The temporary stadium sits in the Long Beach Convention Center lot, with the wall backed by ocean air and a big video screen for replays.
CLB01.potentialContendersIntro: Qualification runs through 2027 and 2028, so the 2028 field is not set. These are projected contenders based on recent results.

potentialContenders.name: Sorato Anraku
potentialContenders.note: Reigning Boulder world champion (2025) and Paris 2024 silver medalist in the combined event. He won five Boulder stops in 2026. Projected favorite if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Lee Dohyun
potentialContenders.note: Ran second in the 2026 Boulder standings before the final stop. Likely contender if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Mejdi Schalck
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world silver medalist and third in the 2026 standings going into Salt Lake City. Could reach the final.

potentialContenders.name: Toby Roberts
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 combined champion. He missed early 2026 events with an injury, so his form is worth watching.

CLB02.blurb:
Speed climbing starts with qualification, and the stopwatch is the story. Men and women both run in this early session. Their times decide the seeding for the head-to-head knockouts.

The records keep falling. China's Zhao Yicheng lowered the men's world record to 4.54 seconds in 2026. American Emma Hunt ran 5.99 in Kraków, the first women's time under six seconds.

The 15-meter wall is a short, loud spectacle. Expect runs to finish in about five or six seconds, with the crowd reacting to every time on the board.
CLB02.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 medalists are confirmed history, but 2028 entries are not. These are projected names for the men's and women's qualification runs.

potentialContenders.name: Zhao Yicheng
potentialContenders.note: Set the men's world record of 4.54 seconds in 2026 and won the series title. Projected favorite if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Sam Watson
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and 2026 Kraków winner with a personal best of 4.60. He could be a home-crowd draw.

potentialContenders.name: Emma Hunt

potentialContenders.name: Aleksandra Mirosław

potentialContenders.name: Desak Made Rita Kusuma Dewi

CLB03.blurb:
The women's Boulder semifinal is the first real test of a new medal event. Only the best climbers move on to the final.

Slovenia's Janja Garnbret has won both Boulder and Lead world titles in 2025 and the combined event at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024. The field is catching up, though. France's Zélia Avezou beat her in Keqiao in 2026.

It is a morning session at the Long Beach waterfront, a good chance to see problem-solving up close before the final.
CLB03.potentialContendersIntro: Women's Boulder is wide open going into 2028. Everyone below is a projected contender, not a confirmed entry.

potentialContenders.name: Janja Garnbret
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 combined champion and 2025 world Boulder champion, with 10 world titles. The projected favorite if she competes.

potentialContenders.name: Zélia Avezou
potentialContenders.note: Beat Garnbret at the 2026 Keqiao season opener. A rising threat.

potentialContenders.name: Oriane Bertone

potentialContenders.name: Erin McNeice
potentialContenders.note: Led the 2026 Boulder standings before the final stop in Salt Lake City. A likely semifinalist if she qualifies.

CLB04.blurb:
Lead climbing gets its own medal for the first time. This semifinal is short, but one fall ends a climber's day.

Each athlete gets one attempt on a tall route. The highest hold reached ranks the field. Lee Dohyun of South Korea won the 2025 world title at home in Seoul. Japan's Neo Suzuki took the 2026 series title.

This is an evening session. Watching a climber push up the wall as the crowd goes quiet is a different experience from the Boulder sessions.
CLB04.potentialContendersIntro: 2028 rosters are not final. These are projected contenders for the men's Lead event based on recent form.

potentialContenders.name: Lee Dohyun

potentialContenders.name: Neo Suzuki

potentialContenders.name: Sorato Anraku

potentialContenders.name: Jakob Schubert

CLB05.blurb:
This single session has men's and women's Speed from the quarterfinals to the medals. It is the most compact and fast-paced medal session on the climbing schedule.

Every race is a head-to-head sprint, and the results are decided in seconds. Zhao Yicheng's 4.54 men's record and Emma Hunt's 5.99 women's record set a high standard for 2028.

The session runs only 90 minutes. The ocean-side stadium gives you a crowd in full voice and a medal ceremony with barely a pause.

CLB06.blurb:
Women's Lead has its own medal event for the first time. This semifinal is the evening step to the final.

Slovenia's Janja Garnbret is the benchmark. She won her 51st series event in Koper in 2026, 33 of them in Lead. Annie Sanders of the USA took the 2026 series title.

In the late afternoon-to-evening slot, expect hush on the wall and noise between climbers.

The first standalone men's Boulder medals are awarded in this final. It is a high-stakes morning session built around four problems.

Japan's Sorato Anraku comes in as a projected favorite if he qualifies. He was 2025 world champion and won five Boulder stops in 2026. He has also won Boulder gold at the 2026 Asian Games.

Boulder finals are intimate. The crowd sits close to the wall, and every top of a problem brings a roar.

Women's Boulder awards standalone medals for the first time. This final is the morning showdown on four problems.

Janja Garnbret won the 2025 world title after Oriane Bertone missed the last top. In 2026, Zélia Avezou beat her in Keqiao, so the field is competitive.

Expect a close-up view of the wall and a crowd that reacts to every attempt.

CLB09.blurb:
Men's Lead medals are awarded as a standalone event for the first time. The afternoon final is one climb to the top.

Each finalist gets a single go on the route. Highest hold reached wins. South Korea's Lee Dohyun is the reigning world champion, and Japan's Neo Suzuki won the 2026 series.

Expect a quiet crowd during each climb and an eruption when a climber hits the top.
CLB09.potentialContendersIntro: 2028 entries are not confirmed. These are projected contenders for the men's Lead final.

potentialContenders.name: Jakob Schubert

CLB10.blurb:
The climbing program ends with the women's Lead final. It is the last medal event at the Long Beach Climbing Theater, and the first time Lead medals are awarded on their own for women.

Janja Garnbret is the projected favorite if she qualifies. She won the 2025 world Lead title and added Lead wins in Innsbruck and Koper in 2026. Annie Sanders of the USA won the 2026 series title.

It is a morning finale with the Pacific behind the wall, a fitting close to six days of climbing.

CRD01.blurb:
Two medal events, one morning: the men's and women's individual time trials run back to back on July 19, with riders leaving alone and racing only the clock. There are no heats, so the fastest time on the day takes gold.

The course is about 35 km, starting at the LA Zoo in Griffith Park and finishing at Griffith Observatory. Organizers call it challenging, and the finish suggests a climb into the hills, though gradients and the full route are still to be published.

The women's race will crown a new champion, since Paris 2024 winner Grace Brown has retired. On the men's side, Remco Evenepoel won in Paris and at the 2025 World Championships, but his 2028 entry is not confirmed.

This is roadside viewing, not a stadium: no fixed seats, and each rider flashes past briefly. Pick a spot on the climb, watch the start-house rituals near the zoo, and follow the times on the big screens.
CRD01.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gave us Remco Evenepoel and Grace Brown as champions, but Brown has retired and no 2028 entries are confirmed. The names below are projections based on past results, mainly for the men's and women's time trials.

CRD02.blurb:
A 150 km sprint from the Pacific shoreline to the hills above the city, the women's road race is a single-day, winner-takes-all showdown. It starts on Venice Beach's Ocean Front Walk and ends at Griffith Observatory.

The finish is a climb of about 3.9 km at roughly 4.9 percent, with steeper pitches near 6.7 percent. That suits punchy climbers and attackers who can arrive at the foot of it with fresh legs. The full route has not yet been published.

The defending champion is American Kristen Faulkner, who won Paris 2024 with a late attack, the first US road race medal since the 1984 Los Angeles Games. Her 2028 participation has not been confirmed.

Fans watch the start from the roadside along the boardwalk, with palm trees, the beach and the Venice street scene behind them. There is no stadium seating, so expect a casual, open-air atmosphere before the peloton rolls out.
CRD02.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gold, silver and bronze went to Faulkner, Vos and Kopecky. For 2028, recent world championship form points to several likely contenders, though no rosters are set.

CRD03.blurb:
The men's road race is the longest single day of the road program: 250 km from the Pacific coast to the hills of Griffith Park. It starts on Venice Beach's Ocean Front Walk and ends at Griffith Observatory.

The finale is a climb of about 3.9 km at an average of 4.9 percent, with steeper stretches near 6.7 percent. The full route has not been published, so the race's shape is still unknown.

The storylines are rich. Remco Evenepoel is the reigning champion in both the road race and time trial. Tadej Pogacar has said he would like to win this race and would tailor his program for it, and the Tour de France finishes July 16, leaving a quick turnaround.

Fans watch the start from the roadside along the boardwalk, with the Pacific, palm trees and Venice's street performers all around. It is a free-flowing, open-air scene rather than a stadium bowl.
CRD03.potentialContendersIntro: Evenepoel won Paris 2024, ahead of French riders Madouas and Laporte. For 2028, recent form suggests a strong field, but no rosters are confirmed.

CSL01.blurb:
Canoe slalom opens on the day of the Opening Ceremony, with men's and women's kayak singles taking two timed runs each down the Oklahoma City channel. It's the first look at who has the course figured out.

Every paddler must thread a series of upstream and downstream gates, and a touched pole or missed gate adds seconds. Heats decide who moves on to the semifinals, so a clean run matters more than raw speed.

The 304.8 m concrete channel drops 5.15 m, with the downtown OKC skyline behind it. Morning starts help with the summer heat, and banks and decks beside the course keep fans close to the gates.

CSL02.blurb:
Women's K1 is one of the first medal events of the Games, with the semifinal and final held back to back on Saturday morning. A medal is decided within a few hours.

The storyline centers on Jessica Fox. She missed 2025 after kidney tumour surgery, then won the 2026 world title on this course, her fifth in the event.

USA's Evy Leibfarth finished 1.31 seconds behind Fox at that worlds, which makes a home-nation medal push a real possibility. Whether either competes in 2028 is not yet confirmed.

Expect a loud crowd along the banks, with the skyline behind the finish and a single, tense run deciding who gets the medal.
CSL02.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gold went to Jess Fox, with Klaudia Zwolinska second and Kimberley Woods third. Projected 2028 contenders below are based on the 2026 worlds and are not confirmed entries.

potentialContenders.name: Jessica Fox

CSL03.blurb:
Men's K1 brings the semifinal and final into one Sunday-morning session, with the field cut quickly and one run deciding the medals. Small time gaps are the norm.

The 2026 worlds on this course showed how tight it can be. Jakub Krejci won in 83.65 seconds, with Michal Pasiut about 0.7 seconds back and Giovanni De Gennaro third.

De Gennaro won Paris 2024 gold, so the field has both a reigning Games champion and a new world champion. Rosters for 2028 are not yet set.

Fans watch from the channel's banks, with the downtown OKC skyline behind the course and a short morning window for the medal run.

CSL04.blurb:
C1 heats begin the canoe events. Paddlers kneel in a single-blade canoe, and each gets two runs to reach the semifinals. Women's and men's fields share this morning session.

Heats are a good way to see the sport at close range. The canoe is harder to control than a kayak, and small slips cost time on every gate.

The session is shorter than the K1 heats, so it is an easy morning to fit in. Watch from the channel banks or the covered patio, with the downtown skyline in view.

CSL05.blurb:
Fox won women's C1 gold in Paris and with it became the first woman to win the canoe-kayak double at a single Games. On July 18 she could try for that again in the C1 semifinal and final.

The Paris podium also included Germany's Elena Lilik and the USA's Evy Leibfarth. A home-nation medal chance adds extra interest for American fans.

Both rounds are packed into a single morning. The 2026 worlds showed Slovakia and the Czech Republic are deep in this event too, so the final could be a wide-open race.

CSL06.blurb:
Men's C1 puts paddlers in a single-blade canoe, kneeling in the boat. The semifinal and final take place on one Wednesday morning, and gate errors can swing the outcome.

The event is open. Miquel Trave of Spain won the 2026 world title on this course in 88.28 seconds, ahead of Britain's Adam Burgess and Lukas Kratochvil of Czechia.

France's Nicolas Gestin, the Paris 2024 champion, won the Prague World Cup in June 2026. That sets up a strong cast for 2028, assuming they qualify.

The course drops 5.15 m, so you'll see boats surge, stall and bounce through the gates with the OKC skyline behind them.

CSL07.blurb:
Kayak cross is the head-to-head format that debuted in Paris 2024. This session opens the knockout with Round 1 and the repechage, so paddlers who stumble early still have a second chance.

Several boats start together from a ramp and race through gates, with contact and strategy part of the show. It's faster and more chaotic than timed slalom.

The 2026 worlds in Oklahoma City drew 77 men from 40 nations, so expect a big field. Both men's and women's races run in this session.

The morning crowd gets the early drama on the banks, with the skyline in the distance.

CSL08.blurb:
Kayak cross heats are the middle step in the knockout, after Round 1 and repechage and before the quarterfinals on finals day. Racing is short but decisive, with only the top finishers advancing.

Four boats go down the channel together, which means tactics matter as much as speed. A good start and clean line through the first gates can decide it.

The 2026 results show deep fields, with Switzerland's Marx siblings, Czech and British men, and French women all in the mix. Their 2028 participation isn't confirmed.

This is a quick morning session, so arrive early to catch every heat from the banks.

CSL09.blurb:
This is the final day of canoe slalom, with kayak cross quarterfinals, semifinals and both medal races in one fast session. Medals are decided by head-to-head finishes, not times.

The field comes from fresh results. Vit Prindis won the 2026 world title by passing Dimitri Marx late, and Alena Marx won the women's title ahead of Noemie Fox.

Paris 2024 champions Finn Butcher and Noemie Fox are the benchmark, and Joe Clarke, a 2026 World Cup winner, adds depth. Who actually qualifies for 2028 is not yet known.

Expect a big crowd at the channel for the last slalom medals, with the OKC skyline behind the finish.

CSP01.blurb:
Canoe sprint opens on the narrow saltwater channel at Marine Stadium. Heats and quarterfinals stack four events into one morning: men's and women's K2 500m, men's C1 1000m and women's C1 200m.

The women's C1 200m is the one to watch. Paris 2024 was decided by 0.01 seconds, and Ukraine's Liudmyla Luzan won the 2026 world title, so the field looks wide open.

The men's C1 1000m brings Martin Fuksa, the Paris champion who tied for 2026 world gold, if he qualifies and competes. Early rounds are an easy way to see the course without a final's price tag.

Spectators watch from the shoreline beside the lanes, with Belmont Shore and the Long Beach skyline in view. The venue also hosted rowing at the 1932 Games.

CSP02.blurb:
This is the first medal session of the canoe sprint program, with semifinals and A finals in three events. Men's and women's K2 500m and the men's C1 1000m all end with medals awarded.

The men's C1 1000m is the longest sprint race on the program. Paris champion Martin Fuksa and Hungary's Daniel Fejes tied for 2026 world gold, and Brazil's Isaquias Queiroz is chasing 2028 as well.

The women's K2 500m is full of questions. Australia's Kailey Harlen and Natalia Drobot are the 2026 world champions, while Lisa Carrington, the Paris gold medalist, says she plans to race in 2028, her fifth Games.

The course is a straight channel with the finish right in front of the shoreline crowd. Expect semifinals and finals back to back through the morning.

Day three is a busy morning of heats and quarterfinals in six events. It covers the K4 500m and C2 500m for men and women, the men's K1 1000m and the women's K1 500m.

The men's K1 1000m has a deep field. Czechia's Josef Dostal won Paris, and Portugal's Fernando Pimenta won the 2026 world title ahead of Hungary's Balint Kopasz.

The women's K1 500m is where Lisa Carrington's name could return. She has said she plans to race in 2028, though she had her first child in October 2026, so her entry is not guaranteed.

This is a good session for fans who like variety, with boats of one, two and four on the water. Seats are along the shoreline, close to the lanes.

Medals go out in the women's K1 500m, the women's C2 500m and the men's K1 1000m. Each event runs semifinals and A finals on the same morning.

The women's K1 500m has an unusual storyline. Lisa Carrington won Paris 2024 in a Games-best time and tied the canoeing record of eight golds. She skipped 2025 and 2026 and has said 2028 is her goal.

The men's K1 1000m looks like a three-way fight. Portugal's Fernando Pimenta won 2026 worlds, with Hungary's Balint Kopasz 0.22 behind and Australia's Thomas Green third. Czechia's Josef Dostal won Paris.

The finals are in the open air next to Alamitos Bay, so you can hear the crowd as boats approach the line.

Canoe sprint ends with four finals: the women's C1 200m, men's C2 500m, and the women's and men's K4 500m. The four-person boats make the closing session loud and fast.

The women's C1 200m is the short-sprint highlight. Katie Vincent won Paris 2024 in a world-record 44.12, just 0.01 ahead of Nevin Harrison, and Ukraine's Liudmyla Luzan won the 2026 worlds.

In the K4 500m, Germany won the Paris men's gold, and New Zealand won the women's gold with Lisa Carrington. She is targeting 2028 but had a child in October 2026, so her lineup spot is unconfirmed.

Expect a festive last morning, with crews lined up side by side along the same channel that hosted rowing in 1932.

CTR01.blurb:
Track cycling opens with a one-hour morning blast: men's and women's team sprint qualifying. Each trio has three laps, and the clock sets the bracket for the afternoon's first round.

The Paris 2024 world records still stand as the marks to watch: 40.949 for the Netherlands men and 45.186 for Great Britain's women. China won the 2026 women's world title in 45.578, so the women's field looks wide open.

Carson Velodrome seats about 2,450 around a 250-meter pine track, and every seat is close to the boards. Expect a quick, loud first look at the banking, with riders hitting roughly 50 mph.

The first medals of track cycling are decided in the team sprint, with the men's and women's first rounds and finals packed into one afternoon. The session also includes men's team pursuit qualifying.

The Netherlands won the men's gold at Paris 2024 and the 2026 world title, with Harrie Lavreysen riding the key leadoff-to-anchor slot. The women's final is more uncertain: Great Britain won in Paris, but China took the 2026 world title.

The team sprint is over in under a minute, so the compact Carson Velodrome keeps the roar close and constant. Startline launches, rapid handoffs and finishing times flashing on the board make it an easy event to follow.

CTR03.blurb:
This is a deep morning session for endurance fans, with women's team pursuit qualifying and the men's team pursuit first round. The women's keirin repechages and men's sprint qualifying round it out.

The team pursuit is a 4,000-meter chase on the 250-meter track. Great Britain's women are the form team, setting a 4:02.808 world record in February 2026 and winning that year's world title.

The United States won Paris 2024 gold but finished ninth in 2026 world qualifying, so the home crowd may be watching for a rebound. Prelims here are an accessible way to see the sport's range, from pursuit chases to fast flying 200s.

The men's team pursuit final headlines the session, supported by early men's sprint rounds and the women's keirin quarterfinals. It's a full afternoon with a medal on the line.

Australia took Paris 2024 gold over Great Britain after a world record in the heats. Denmark has won the last two world titles, so the 2028 final looks like a real test of who has the depth.

The keirin quarterfinals bring a different kind of drama: a pacing motorbike, six riders and a sprint for position. In this small velodrome, it's close, fast racing without a bad seat.

A packed Thursday has three medal events: the women's team pursuit final, the men's omnium and the women's keirin final. The men's sprint 1/8 and quarterfinals add more racing.

The omnium's four events (scratch, tempo, elimination and points) run in one day, which rewards riders who can do everything. Iuri Leitao has won the 2026 world title and took silver at Paris 2024.

The women's team pursuit could be a showdown after Great Britain's 2026 world title and the US win in Paris. At Carson, expect plenty of changing storylines.

CTR06.blurb:
The men's sprint semifinals are the main draw: best-of-three match sprints where tactics matter as much as speed. Women's sprint qualifying and the 1/32 round fill out the morning.

Harrie Lavreysen has won eight consecutive world sprint titles through 2026, and is unbeaten at Worlds since 2019. Matt Richardson beat him at the 2026 Europeans and holds the flying 200m world record of 8.857.

Richardson's status for 2028 is unresolved after he was withdrawn from Britain's 2026 Worlds squad amid a misconduct investigation. At Carson, riders circle slowly in a cat-and-mouse standoff before the sudden explosive sprint.

A big medal session on Friday: the men's sprint final and the women's madison final. The women's sprint 1/16 round fills out the program.

The sprint final is a best-of-three duel. Harrie Lavreysen beat Leigh Hoffman 2-0 for the 2026 world title, and could be chasing another gold in Los Angeles if he competes.

The madison is a points race where partners tag in with hand slings. Italy won in Paris, while Great Britain's Anna Morris and Erin Boothman won the 2026 world title, so a lively contest at Carson is likely.

Saturday's headline is the men's madison final, a long and chaotic points race that keeps the whole track in motion. The women's sprint 1/8 and quarterfinals and the men's keirin first round run alongside.

Denmark's Carl-Frederik Bevort and Lasse Norman Leth won the 2026 world title with 88 points. Portugal won in Paris, and Iuri Leitao and Ivo Oliveira took 2026 world silver.

In the women's sprint, Yuan Liying won the 2026 world title, while Ellesse Andrews, the Paris 2024 champion, did not reach the podium. At Carson, the madison's sprints and laps gained are easy to follow from any seat.

CTR09.blurb:
The final session of track cycling closes the program with the women's sprint final, the men's keirin final and the women's omnium. It's the last chance to see Carson's banking in action.

Harrie Lavreysen won the 2026 world keirin title and the Paris 2024 gold, and could finish the track program with another if he competes. Yuan Liying beat Emma Finucane 2-0 in the 2026 world sprint final.

The omnium could bring Anna Morris, the 2026 world champion, and possibly Jennifer Valente, the Paris 2024 winner, if she is on the US roster. The keirin's motorbike pace and sudden sprint make a strong finish at Carson.

Diving at the 2028 Games opens with the women's 3m springboard preliminary, a long morning of crisp, quick entries as the field is sorted for the semifinal.

Chen Yiwen won Paris 2024 gold and then won the 2026 Asian Games title, so China arrives as the team to catch. Great Britain's Andrea Spendolini-Sirieix, a former platform diver, says she is aiming to qualify on springboard.

The pool sits open-air in the Arroyo Seco canyon in Pasadena, with Brookside Park's hills behind the well. A 10 AM start means cool morning light and an easy way to see the whole field.

Chen Yiwen is the Paris 2024 gold medalist and added 2026 Asian Games gold on 3m, plus synchro gold with new partner Chen Jia. Whether the same names are in Pasadena is still to be decided.

Expect a focused crowd at the Rose Bowl Aquatics Center, with the late-morning sun on the springboards and the first real tension of the event.

The women's 3m springboard final is the first individual diving medals of the Games, and it sets the tone for the whole week.

Chen Yiwen won Paris 2024 gold and won again at the 2026 Asian Games, so she would be the one to beat if she is on the board. Maddison Keeney's Paris silver kept Australia in the picture.

The final starts at 3:30 PM in the open-air well beneath the Arroyo Seco hills. Expect a loud, flag-waving crowd and a quick 75-minute session with medals on every dive.

The men's 3m springboard preliminary is a morning primer for one of diving's best rivalries. China's Paris 2024 medalists meet a Mexican world champion on the way to the semifinal.

Xie Siyi won gold at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024. Osmar Olvera is the reigning world champion and won three golds at the 2026 Central American and Caribbean Games.

Early-session crowds at the Rose Bowl Aquatics Center are relaxed, so it's a good chance to see the springboard's big names up close. Whether they all qualify is still to be decided.

The men's 3m springboard semifinal is the last cut before the medal round, and the standard is high. Divers fly off the board at a steady, demanding pace.

Xie Siyi and Wang Zongyuan went one-two in Paris 2024, with Osmar Olvera of Mexico in third. Olvera is the reigning world champion, so this round could preview a three-way final.

The session runs 3:30 to 5:30 PM, as afternoon sun hits the open-air pool in Brookside Park. It's a good value ticket for hearing the crowd react to every near-perfect entry.

The men's 3m springboard final could again pit China against Mexico. In Paris 2024, Osmar Olvera was the only non-Chinese medalist here.

Xie Siyi won his second straight title and Wang Zongyuan took silver. Olvera has since become world champion, though 2028 rosters are not settled.

The final starts at 3:30 PM in the open-air Rose Bowl Aquatics Center. Expect Mexican fans to be loud, and scores to be tight over five rounds with little room for error.

The women's 10m platform preliminary has a major question: will Quan Hongchan be back? She won gold at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024.

Quan missed China's 2026 Asian Games trials with tibia and ankle injuries and has spoken publicly about the pressure after Paris. Teammate Chen Yuxi, Paris silver medalist, is a key figure.

The platform tower stands over the Rose Bowl pool's open-air setting, and a morning prelim puts you close to the action. Seats are more relaxed than at the medal rounds.

Quan Hongchan and Chen Yuxi went one-two in Paris 2024. With Quan sidelined by injuries in 2026, Chen Yuxi carried China's platform load at the 2026 trials.

The session starts at 3:30 PM, with the afternoon sun on the tower and the pool. Expect gasps from the stands at each near-vertical rip entry.

The men's 10m platform preliminary opens an event that China doesn't always win. Cao Yuan took Paris 2024 gold, but reigning world champion Yang Hao finished only 12th.

Australia's Cassiel Rousseau is the current world champion. Japan's Rikuto Tamai and Britain's Noah Williams took silver and bronze in Paris, and the event feels wide open.

Morning sessions at the Rose Bowl Aquatics Center let you watch the full field at an easy pace, with the hills of Brookside Park behind the 10m tower.

The 3:30 PM final in open-air Pasadena is a short, high-stakes session, with the tower silhouetted against the afternoon sky and the crowd hushed before each dive.

The event has had many winners: Matthew Mitcham in 2008, David Boudia in 2012, and Cao Yuan in Paris. Cassiel Rousseau is now world champion, and Tom Daley has retired.

The final follows later the same day. Come in the morning at the Rose Bowl Aquatics Center to see who survives, with Canada's synchro bronze pair also in the mix.

The final runs 3:30 to 4:45 PM in the open-air Rose Bowl Aquatics Center. Twelve divers get six rounds from 10 meters in the Pasadena afternoon, with medals on every dive.

Chen Yiwen and Chang Yani won gold in Paris 2024. Chen Yiwen has since won the 2026 Asian Games title with new partner Chen Jia. The United States took silver in Paris and will be at home.

The 11:30 AM start in Pasadena brings late-morning light and a likely lively home crowd. Pairs are judged on matching timing, so even tiny gaps in rhythm show up in the scores.

North Korea took silver in Paris and again in 2026, and Britain's Paris bronze pair will not return. Doors open for a 2 PM final in open-air Pasadena.

DIV16.blurb:
Eleven dives' worth of nerve, compressed into a single final: the men's synchronized 10m platform is decided in one hour, with no semifinal safety net. Two divers, one platform, and the judges are watching for matching entries, mid-air timing and splashes that mirror each other.

China took gold at Paris 2024 with Lian Junjie and Yang Hao, but Great Britain won this event at Tokyo 2020 and took silver in Paris. Tom Daley has retired, so Noah Williams may need a new partner.

The pairings are not yet set. Teams will be determined through Diving World Cup Stops 1 and 2 in 2028, so the lineup will take shape only months before the Games.

The Rose Bowl Aquatics Center is an open-air pool in the Arroyo Seco, with the hills of Brookside Park behind the tower. A 4:00 PM start means afternoon California sun on the platform, and a small crowd will react to every near-perfect entry.

The equestrian program opens on a Saturday morning at Santa Anita Park, with the first eventing dressage tests of the Games. It is the quiet first act of a long three-day format.

Dressage sets the leaderboard before cross-country. Michael Jung won the 2026 world title on FischerChipmunk FRH, but that horse was retired in November 2026, so his 2028 mount is an open question.

Expect a hushed, tailored atmosphere in the historic grandstand, with the San Gabriel Mountains behind the arena. Santa Anita also hosted equestrian in 1984, which adds some history to the setting.

Day 1 of eventing dressage ends with an evening session at Santa Anita Park. Dressage scores here become the penalty points that riders carry into cross-country.

This is where record scores have been set recently. Jung and Laura Collett both posted record eventing dressage marks at Paris 2024, so a low, hard-to-catch number is possible.

It is a calm late-afternoon session, with riders in tailcoats and long shadows over the infield. It suits spectators who like technical sport and a slow build.

The weekend setting suits a relaxed morning at Santa Anita. Watch for the rider and horse pairs who are close on points, since cross-country can reshuffle the order.

Spectators should expect a temporary course on a Thoroughbred racetrack, a different feel from a typical cross-country venue. The crowd follows each round on a big screen and cheers from the grandstand.

The session runs into the night at Santa Anita Park. It is a long, high-stakes evening with a medal ceremony at the end.

Germany won team gold at Aachen 2026 and holds the Paris 2024 team title. Jessica von Bredow-Werndl missed Aachen when Times Kismet went into quarantine, so her status is worth watching.

Flag football's first day as a medal sport starts here, the afternoon after the opening ceremony. Three games, men's and women's, kick off a tournament that has never existed at a Summer Games.

Each side fields five players, and games run two 20-minute halves. The full matchups are not set, because the last three berths per gender are decided at June 2028 qualifiers in Montreal and Orlando.

FFB14.blurb:
The closing session of the flag football tournament hands out the first women's medals in the sport's Games history, with bronze and gold games on the final day.

Canada, the reigning world champions, beat the U.S. 27-20 in 2026, ending a three-title U.S. run. Mexico, the 2025 World Games champions, make this a legitimately open field.

Saturday afternoon at Exposition Park Stadium should be a celebration, with the Coliseum next door and a crowd that has watched the sport grow from nothing at the Games.

GAR01.blurb:
The first gymnastics session of the 2028 Games opens a full Saturday of men's qualification at DTLA Arena. It is the earliest look at who arrives sharp.

Qualification sets the fields for the men's team final, the all-around and the eight-man apparatus finals. Each nation can bring at most one team of five, with no reserves, so one miss counts.

Expect a steep indoor bowl in downtown Los Angeles, with upper-level seats looking straight down on the floor. A morning prelim is an easy, affordable way to see world-class gymnastics up close.
GAR01.potentialContendersIntro: Rosters for 2028 are not set, and subdivision assignments are not confirmed. Based on 2025-2026 form, these gymnasts could appear in Saturday's qualification rounds, though not necessarily in this session.

potentialContenders.note: Won his fourth straight world all-around title in 2026; projected to compete if selected for Japan's team.

GAR02.blurb:
The middle of three men's qualification blocks on opening Saturday, this is the afternoon heat. Every routine feeds the team, all-around and apparatus final fields.

The Paris 2024 podiums mean little here, because only the top qualifiers move on. The sport's pommel horse and vault specialists are especially worth watching, since one clean set can earn a final spot.

The setting is downtown's L.A. Live district, with restaurants next door and the Metro stop at Pico nearby. You can make a full day of it between sessions.

GAR03.blurb:
The night session closes men's qualification and sets the lineup for the team final on July 17 and the all-around final on July 19. Whoever makes the cut here moves into medal rounds.

The new mixed team event may also draw on these scores. The format trialed at the 2025 European Championships sent the top 16 pairs from qualification to the final, though FIG has not set the 2028 format.

A 7:30 PM start under the arena lights suits a big-crowd feel. Routines on parallel bars, rings and high bar play well in the steep bowl.
GAR03.potentialContendersIntro: No 2028 rosters exist yet. These gymnasts are projections based on 2026 world apparatus results and could appear in the evening block if they qualify.

GAR04.blurb:
Women's gymnastics begins Sunday morning with the first two of five qualification subdivisions. It is the first look at the field chasing Paris 2024's champions.

These scores decide the team final, all-around and apparatus fields. The United States, China and Japan already hold team spots, while nine more teams are still to be decided in 2027.

Simone Biles has not announced whether she will compete in 2028, so any appearance is far from confirmed. Either way, a morning start at DTLA Arena puts you close to the early action.
GAR04.potentialContendersIntro: Rosters are not set, and subdivision assignments have not been confirmed. These are projected names based on 2025-2026 results.

potentialContenders.name: Skye Blakely
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 world all-around title; a projected U.S. leader if she makes the team.

potentialContenders.name: Kaylia Nemour
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 uneven bars champion who won bars and beam at the 2026 Worlds.

potentialContenders.name: Angelina Melnikova
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 world all-around and 2026 European all-around as a neutral athlete; 2028 eligibility is unconfirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Simone Biles
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 all-around and vault champion, undecided on 2028 as of late September 2026; appearance is speculative.

GAR05.blurb:
A shorter midafternoon block, Women's Qualification 3 packs a lot into under two hours. It could be one of the most closely watched sessions of the day.

Rebeca Andrade is a storyline to follow. She took 2025 off, returned in 2026 and says she will skip floor, focusing on vault and beam with bars to follow in 2027.

Brazil's women finished fifth at the 2026 Worlds, so their team must still qualify. The compact timing makes this a good session for fans who want a quick, high-quality look at the sport.
GAR05.potentialContendersIntro: Rosters and subdivisions are not confirmed for 2028, so these are projections. The names come from the 2026 World Championships vault and beam podiums.

GAR06.blurb:
Women's Qualification 4 is the evening heat, when the arena fills and the stakes feel higher. The apparatus final fields are taking shape.

Twelve women's teams are expected in total: China, the United States and Japan are in, and nine more will come from the 2027 Worlds. Individual spots also come from World Cup series and continental championships.

The building has a long history of big nights, from Lakers championship runs to Grammy telecasts. Gymnastics under those lights should feel just as charged.
GAR06.potentialContendersIntro: These are projections, not confirmed entries, for beam and bars specialists with recent strong form. Italy's team spot, for example, still depends on 2027 qualification.

GAR07.blurb:
The late-night finale of qualification closes out the Sunday marathon. When it ends, the women's team, all-around and apparatus final fields will be set.

If FIG adopts a qualification-based format, mixed team qualifiers will also be decided here. The format trialed at the 2025 Europeans used one man and one woman per nation.

A 9:25 PM start suits the arena's after-dark energy. Plan your ride home around the Metro A and E lines at Pico, since the session runs until about 11 PM.
GAR07.potentialContendersIntro: No 2028 roster is official, and subdivision assignments are not confirmed. These all-around and floor contenders are projected from 2025-2026 results.

GAR08.blurb:
The men's team final is the first artistic gymnastics medal event of the 2028 Games. Five gymnasts per team, no reserves, and a rotation through all six apparatus.

Japan won gold at Paris 2024 ahead of China and the United States, and took the 2026 world title despite misses on parallel bars and high bar. Daiki Hashimoto closed on high bar to seal it.

Expect a loud Monday evening in the DTLA bowl, with the pommel horse often drawing the biggest hush. Every rotation can swing the standings.

GAR09.blurb:
The women's team final is a prime-time Tuesday showdown with a big storyline: can the United States defend Paris 2024 gold? ESPN has described the U.S. as heavy favorites for 2028, based on depth.

That edge is not assured. China beat the United States by 0.233 at the 2026 Worlds, with Japan third, and all three hold 2028 spots.

The arena's steep seating makes this a premium atmosphere. Simone Biles has not announced a 2028 decision, which keeps this session in the spotlight.

GAR10.blurb:
The men's all-around final crowns the sport's most complete gymnast over six apparatus. It is a Wednesday evening of high drama.

Daiki Hashimoto, Japan's four-time reigning world champion, is chasing Kohei Uchimura's record of six straight world titles. Paris 2024 champion Shinnosuke Oka fell twice at the 2026 Worlds and missed the podium.

A Japan-China duel looks likely based on 2024-2026 results. With only one title at stake, the arena feels sharp and focused from the first rotation.

The women's all-around final is Thursday night, and Simone Biles's status could dominate the headlines. She won in Paris 2024 but had not decided on 2028 as of late 2026.

Skye Blakely won the 2026 world title, and the U.S. has had a woman on every world and Games all-around podium since 2003. Rebeca Andrade has said she plans to compete in 2028.

Expect a big, loud, full arena and a close race across vault, bars, beam and floor. This could be one of the most closely watched sessions of the program.

This is the first of three apparatus final sessions on the schedule. FIG has not yet confirmed which apparatus will be in each session, so the exact lineup is still open.

Apparatus finals are the best place to see specialists on a single event, with eight finalists each. Men and women are both part of the program, so expect a mix of events across the three days.

The session runs from late morning to mid-afternoon, so it is an easy daytime ticket. Floor, vault, bars and pommel horse are all possible depending on the final schedule.

The second apparatus final session spans a late-morning slot on Sunday. FIG has not confirmed which events are in each session, so treat the events as undecided.

The 2026 Worlds hint at the stories to follow. Beam, parallel bars and vault all had tight finishes, including Nemour beating Zhang Qingying on a tiebreak.

The daytime crowd usually includes many families and gymnastics fans, and the arena keeps an intimate feel. Each routine stands alone, with the scoreboard moving after every gymnast.
