Apparatus finals bring the sport's specialists to center stage, with a mix of men's and women's events across the final days of competition. This session is on Monday, July 24.

The exact apparatus for each of the three final sessions has not been published. Floor and high bar are strong possibilities for story, but treat that as speculation until the schedule is set.

These are quick, single-routine showdowns, so the crowd noise rises with each one. A single session can offer a full medal race on several apparatus.

GAR15.blurb:
A new medal event for 2028, the Mixed Team Final pairs men and women in one gymnastics contest, taking the program from 14 to 15 medals.

The format and duration are still pending FIG approval, so details could change. A trial at the 2025 European Championships sent the top 16 qualifying pairs to the final, with one man and one woman per nation.

Expect a novel atmosphere at DTLA Arena. Fans will be seeing a gymnastics format that is brand new on the Games stage, so the rules may need explaining as it goes.

GLF01.blurb:
The men's golf tournament opens at Riviera, where 60 players start a four-day, 72-hole chase for a gold medal. It is a long first day with early tee times and plenty of walking.

Defending champion Scottie Scheffler is projected to lead the American group if he qualifies, and he arrives as the Paris 2024 gold medalist. Tommy Fleetwood and Hideki Matsuyama, silver and bronze in Paris, could also return.

Riviera is a walk-the-course venue in a canyon off Sunset Boulevard, with fans spread along the fairways instead of in one big stand. Nobody wins on Thursday's opening day, but you can pick a group and follow it across the hillside.

GLF02.blurb:
Round 2 is where the 60-man men's field starts to separate, and it is the first real cut of nerve at Riviera. There is no official cut in the standard sense, but scores begin to shape the weekend.

Scottie Scheffler's own history is a useful guide. He started slowly in Paris 2024 before closing with a 62, and his 2026 opening rounds ran almost 1.75 strokes higher than his final rounds.

On the ground, this is a day to pick a hole and settle in. The canyon setting and slopes around the finishing holes give you good spots to watch several groups pass.

GLF03.blurb:
Moving day at Riviera sets the 54-hole leaderboard, and the medal picture becomes clearer. The leaders will be known by early evening, while others are still fighting to get into position.

Paris 2024 showed how little a third-round lead can mean. Jon Rahm and Xander Schauffele shared it, and both missed the podium while Scottie Scheffler charged from behind.

Expect big crowds around the closing holes, where the hillside clubhouse overlooks the 18th green and the slopes form a natural amphitheater. A strong Friday score here can turn into a gold-medal Saturday.

GLF04.blurb:
This is the final round and the men's medals are decided at Riviera. Players finish 72 holes and one of them leaves with the gold.

Scottie Scheffler won Paris 2024 with a closing 62, including a back-nine 29. Tommy Fleetwood took silver by one shot, and no man has won back-to-back individual golds since golf returned in 2016.

That gives this round an extra edge: Scheffler would be trying to do something no men's champion has done. If he qualifies, he arrives with four career majors and a second FedEx Cup.

Expect a loud finish around the 18th green, with fans on the hillside below the clubhouse. A statue of Ben Hogan stands near the finishing hole.

GLF05.blurb:
This is the first-ever golf mixed-team session at the Games. Sixteen national teams, each with one man and one woman, play 18 holes of four-ball, where both players hit and the better score counts.

It is a quick format, so a few hot putts can change the standings. The same teams then play foursomes the next day to decide the medals.

At Riviera, expect fans spread along the fairways in the canyon setting rather than packed into a single stand. As a new medal event, it feels like an early look at something fresh.

GLF06.blurb:
The first golf mixed-team medals at the Games are decided in an 18-hole foursomes round. It is also golf's first team medal event since 1904.

In foursomes, partners alternate shots with one ball, so the format rewards trust and steady nerves. One bad hole can undo a good start, and the four-ball leaders from Sunday do not have a safe cushion.

The session is a morning-to-early-afternoon affair at Riviera, with fans following pairings through the canyon and gathering near the hillside finish. It is a good option if you want a golf medal ceremony without a full-day commitment.

GLF07.blurb:
The women's tournament begins at Riviera, with 60 players starting a four-day, 72-hole chase for gold. Opening day is a chance to see the field up close before the leaderboard tightens.

Lydia Ko is the defending champion after winning Paris 2024 gold, and Riviera should feel familiar to many players after the 2026 U.S. Women's Open was held there.

Nelly Korda won that Open at 8 under, though she opened with a 73 and was tied for 56th. That is a reminder that a slow first round does not end a title run.

GLF08.blurb:
Round 2 of the women's event gives the field a second look at Riviera before the weekend. It is a good day to watch players adjust to the course's slopes and tricky greens.

Lydia Ko, the defending champion, owns a silver from 2016, a bronze from Tokyo and the Paris 2024 gold. In 2026 she shot a career-low 60 in the opening round of the Ford Championship.

Expect a relaxed walking atmosphere around the course. The hillside setting is good for a long day in the sun with a clear view of players heading toward the closing holes.

Round 3 of the women's tournament sets the 54-hole standings before the medal round. It is a good day to watch leaders protect position and chasers push for a breakthrough.

Lydia Ko is the reigning champion, and the field may include players who already played the mixed-team event at Riviera earlier in the week.

The canyon setting and hillside finish give the late afternoon a gathering feel. Expect fans to start concentrating around the 17th and 18th holes as the leaderboard narrows.

GLF10.blurb:
The women's final round at Riviera decides the individual medals and closes the golf program. It is the last chance to see world-class golf at the Games.

Lydia Ko is the defending champion, and her Paris 2024 gold completed a set of medals. Nelly Korda, the 2020 champion, won the 2026 U.S. Women's Open at Riviera by one stroke after a birdie on the 17th.

The finish is set against the hillside clubhouse above the 18th green, where the slopes form a natural amphitheater. It is a fitting backdrop for a medal round with several former champions possibly in the mix.

GRY01.blurb:
The first of two qualification sessions opens the individual rhythmic competition at the Galen Center. It is an easy way to see a wide field of gymnasts before the top 10 are set for the final.

Each gymnast performs four apparatus routines, and combined scores across both sessions decide who advances. Up to 24 gymnasts compete, with a maximum of two per nation.

The Galen Center is a compact two-deck arena of about 10,000 seats, so even upper rows sit fairly close to the floor. Expect a lively afternoon crowd and a steady stream of routines from morning-to-evening start orders.
GRY01.potentialContendersIntro: Rosters for 2028 are not set, so these names are projections based on recent World Championship results. Nations earn places through the 2026 and 2027 Worlds and other qualifiers.

GRY02.blurb:
The second qualification session closes out the individual qualifying day. By the end of it, the full field has performed and the top 10 for the all-around final are decided.

The stakes are real: one drop or a missed catch can end a medal hopeful's run. Combined scores from both sessions set the final standings across all four apparatus.

The evening session at the Galen Center should feel energetic, with USC-area crowds filing in near the Jefferson/USC Metro station. The compact bowl keeps the action close, which suits rhythmic's fine details.

GRY03.blurb:
Group qualification brings the five-gymnast teams to the floor, where synchronized throws and catches make for a very different show from the individual events. The top groups move on to the next day's final.

Groups perform two routines, five balls and a mixed hoops-and-clubs routine, built on tight formations and high-risk exchanges. One lost apparatus can swing a ranking.

The Galen Center's close-in seating suits group work, where the patterns across the floor are as much a part of the show as the individual skills. It is a good session for fans who like precision and teamwork.

The individual all-around final is the headline rhythmic session of the Games. Ten gymnasts each perform four routines, and the combined total decides the gold, silver and bronze medals.

Paris 2024 gold medalist Darja Varfolomeev of Germany has won three straight world all-around titles. If she competes, the chase for her from Bulgaria's Stiliana Nikolova and Italy's Sofia Raffaeli could make for a tight contest.

The Galen Center should be loud on a Friday evening, with the audience close to the floor for every ball catch and ribbon flourish. Seats near the floor give a clear view of the footwork and the apparatus work.

The group all-around final is the last rhythmic gymnastics medal event of the 2028 Games. Five-gymnast teams compete in one decisive session with a medal on the line.

China won Paris 2024 gold, its first in the sport, ahead of Israel and Italy. Since then, Japan, Brazil and Spain have filled the world podium in 2025 and 2026, so the order could be hard to call.

A Saturday afternoon at the Galen Center should offer a charged finish to the rhythmic program. With the arena's seating close to the floor, the group's synchronized throws and catches are easy to follow.

GTR01.blurb:
Trampoline's men's competition packs qualification and the medal final into one afternoon, so you can watch the field get cut and the champion crowned in under three hours.

The rivalry is already set. Belarus's Ivan Litvinovich won Paris 2024 gold, and reports say he beat China's Wang Zisai for the 2026 world title. Wang had beaten him earlier that year in Alkmaar.

Expect the usual format of a qualification round and then a final, with judges scoring difficulty, execution and time in the air. Japan's Hayato Miyano is pushing difficulty with triple-flip routines.

Inside DTLA Arena, the steep bowl puts even upper-level seats almost directly above the bed. Watch the athletes climb in height for every skill. Eligibility terms for Russian and Belarusian athletes at the 2028 Games had not been confirmed.

GTR02.blurb:
The women's trampoline final is an evening headliner. Qualification and the medal round run back to back, so the night builds toward a single decisive set of routines.

The field looks wide open. Great Britain's Bryony Page won Paris 2024 gold, but she will be 37 by 2028 and had not publicly confirmed her plans. China's Hu Yicheng won the 2025 world title.

The 2026 Worlds added more names. Belarus's Viyaleta Bardzilouskaya took silver, Japan's Tanaka Kiko took bronze and China won the team title. Neutral athletes also led the 2026 European Championships.

In the DTLA Arena bowl, the evening lighting and the steep seating should make each ten-bounce routine feel close to the action. Eligibility terms for Russian and Belarusian athletes at the 2028 Games had not been confirmed.

HBL01.blurb:
The men's handball tournament starts here. The first morning of play in Long Beach comes two days before the Opening Ceremony, with two preliminary matches back to back.

Twelve teams are split into two groups of six playing round robins, and the top four in each group reach the quarterfinals. Every early result matters, which makes the opening day a lively one.

The drum-shaped arena sits by the harbor, and its exterior carries Wyland's giant whale mural. Inside, the building will be set up for about 12,000 fans, so even a morning game should feel loud.

Croatia reached the 2025 world final and Denmark beat them 32-26 there. Teams like that, plus Spain, could show up in the group stage if they qualify.

The arena is a 1962 building on the downtown waterfront that hosted volleyball at the 1984 Games. After the final whistle, the harbor setting makes for an easy walk out.

Norway is the team everyone has to chase after winning Paris 2024 and the 2025 world title. Henny Reistad, a three-time IHF Female World Player of the Year, could lead the way if she plays.

Host USA is guaranteed a women's place, and a home crowd could make early sessions lively.

Seats in a 12,000-capacity arena are never far from the court, so a mid-afternoon session still carries real noise.

The final women's quarterfinal closes the day in prime time, deciding the last semifinal spot. After this match, the semifinal field is set.

Germany is a projected contender after reaching the 2025 world final, where it lost to Norway 23-20. It would need to qualify first, which is not guaranteed.

The evening atmosphere at Long Beach Arena should be at its peak, with about 12,000 seats and a drum-shaped hall that holds in the noise.

HBL39.blurb:
The first men's semifinal puts a gold medal match one win away. The winners advance to the final on 27 July, while the losers drop into the bronze match.

Denmark has beaten Germany in two straight major finals, 39-26 at Paris 2024 and 34-27 at the 2026 Euro. A rematch is a possible storyline, though no 2028 pairings are set.

Semifinals at Long Beach Arena bring the sharpest atmosphere of the men's event, with about 12,000 fans packed tightly around the court.

HBL40.blurb:
One win from a gold medal match: the second men's semifinal at Long Beach Arena sends one team into the final and the other into a bronze medal game. Expect a hard-edged, high-scoring afternoon.

Denmark won Paris 2024 gold by beating Germany 39-26, then beat Germany again 34-27 in the 2026 European final. Who reaches this semifinal is still open, but Denmark is a projected contender if it qualifies.

The field is built through continental and spring 2028 qualifiers. Croatia, 2025 world silver medalists, and Spain, the Paris 2024 bronze medalists, are among the teams that could be in the mix.

Inside the round, drum-shaped arena on the Long Beach waterfront, about 12,000 fans will sit close to the court. Handball is loud and fast, with goals coming every few seconds and the crowd rising with every steal and fast break.

HBL41.blurb:
One of two women's semifinals, with a gold medal match at stake. Norway and the other top teams will treat this as the real finish line.

Norway won Paris 2024 gold and the 2025 Worlds, its fifth world title, more than any other team. In 2025 it beat the Netherlands 35-25 in the semifinals, a result that shows how hard it is to catch.

Long Beach Arena will be full for a morning semifinal. The host United States women are also in the field, and the arena will back them if they are still playing.

HBL42.blurb:
The second women's semifinal pushes two teams toward the gold medal match. For many fans it may be the best women's game in the building all week.

France won the 2023 world title, then Germany knocked it out of the 2025 semifinals. Germany went on to lose the final 23-20 to Norway in Rotterdam.

Henny Reistad is set to join Brest from summer 2027, so she should be familiar with French hardwood before arriving. In a round arena by the harbor, the game could turn on one goalkeeper or one hot shooter.

The men's bronze medal match is the last game for the semifinal losers, and the medal they take home is the one they will remember. Teams that arrive here often play with more freedom than you might expect.

Spain won bronze at Paris 2024, so the bracket has a precedent. Germany, Croatia and France are among the teams that might be fighting for third if they qualify.

The session runs in the morning before the gold medal match on the same Thursday. You can see both games at Long Beach Arena, a venue that is a short walk from the water.

The men's gold medal match is the final session of the men's tournament. A full house in Long Beach will decide the men's handball champion of the 2028 Games.

Denmark is the Paris 2024 champion, the 2025 world champion for a fourth straight time, and the 2026 European champion. Germany lost to the Danes in both the Paris 2024 and 2026 Euros finals, so a rematch would have a story attached.

Mathias Gidsel will be 29 and is projected to be the center of attention if Denmark qualifies. The arena's roughly 12,000 seats will make the final loud and close.

HBL45.blurb:
The women's bronze medal match is the last game for the women's semifinal losers. Both teams have a medal on the line, and the stands should be lively.

Denmark took bronze at Paris 2024, which gave the country medals in both the men's and women's tournaments. Germany, France and the Netherlands are among the teams that could land here if they qualify.

The host U.S. women are still building through a national residency program in Florida under coach Sarah Gascon, so a bronze game is a long way off. For the neutral fan, this is a morning match at a harbor-side arena with a great view.

The final handball match of the 2028 Games awards women's gold at Long Beach Arena. It closes out the sport's tournament with a full house of roughly 12,000 expected inside the venue.

Norway won Paris 2024 by beating France 29-21, and then took a record fifth world title in 2025 by beating Germany 23-20 in Rotterdam. Whether they can repeat is the big storyline, though nothing is guaranteed over a 2028 knockout run.

The arena is a drum-shaped 1962 building on the Long Beach waterfront, wrapped in Wyland's giant Planet Ocean whale mural. Expect a loud, close-in indoor crowd, with fans from European handball nations mixing with curious Southern California locals.

Hockey opens at Carson Field with a double bill of men's pool matches. It is the first look at the new 12-team format, where pool placings now decide who skips the play-in round.

The Netherlands arrive as defending champions after beating Germany in a Paris 2024 shoot-out. Exact pairings depend on the draw, but the host U.S. men have a confirmed place in the field.

The primary pitch is listed at about 15,000 seats, mostly temporary stands. A morning start in Carson should feel like opening day, with the whole complex warming up.

The Paris 2024 podium of the Netherlands, Germany and India looms over the field. Germany beat the Dutch in a shoot-out at the 2025 European final, so the rivalry is fresh.

The night session lets fans catch a full evening of hockey in the South Bay, with a pitch-side atmosphere closer to a big club night than a stuffy arena.

potentialContenders.name: Argentina

potentialContenders.name: Belgium

potentialContenders.name: USA

HOC17.blurb:
Friday morning brings two more women's pool matches, with the group tables starting to take shape. Each result moves teams toward a direct quarterfinal spot or the July 23 play-in.

The new format raises the cost of a slow start. A team that stumbles in the pool must win an extra knockout match just to reach the last eight.

The morning slot at Carson Field is bright and open-air, and the temporary stands put fans close to the pitch. It is a relaxed way to catch elite hockey before the day heats up.
HOC17.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 medalists the Netherlands, China and Argentina, plus hosts the USA, are among the likely names. The exact matchups depend on the pool draw.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands
potentialContenders.note: Defending champions and Pro League winners in 2024-25 and 2025-26. They could appear if their pool match falls in this slot.

potentialContenders.name: Argentina
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 World Cup, beating the Netherlands on a shoot-out in the final. They are projected as a top contender.

potentialContenders.name: China
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists, who led the final for most of the match. They are a possible presence in this session.

potentialContenders.name: Belgium
potentialContenders.note: Third at the 2026 World Cup and in the 2025-26 Pro League. Charlotte Englebert, the World Cup's best player, is a name to watch.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Automatic qualifiers as hosts. They could play in front of a home crowd if scheduled here.

HOC18.blurb:
This evening session closes out the women's pool stage, and the stakes are at their highest. Teams are fighting to skip the play-in round and book a quarterfinal place outright.

Under the new 2028 format, eight teams that miss a direct quarterfinal spot play for four remaining places. Late pool games can decide who gets a rest day and who plays one more must-win match.

An evening start at Carson Field means cooler air and a louder crowd in the temporary stands. Final pool matches usually bring the most urgency.
HOC18.potentialContendersIntro: The top of the women's game looks settled on recent form, but 2028 qualification runs to March 2028. These are projected contenders, not confirmed entries.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands
potentialContenders.note: Defending champions with six Pro League titles overall. Likely to be in the field as 2025-26 Pro League winners.

potentialContenders.name: Argentina
potentialContenders.note: 2026 World Cup winners on a shoot-out against the Netherlands, and two-time Pro League runners-up. Projected as a top contender.

potentialContenders.name: Australia
potentialContenders.note: Fourth at the 2026 World Cup after a 1-0 bronze-match loss to Belgium. They could be in the field if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Belgium
potentialContenders.note: Beat Australia 1-0 for 2026 World Cup bronze. They are a likely contender if they qualify.

HOC19.blurb:
The play-in round is the biggest change to the 2028 hockey format, and this is its first men's session. Eight teams that missed a direct quarterfinal spot play for four places.

Every match is a straight knockout. Win and you are in the last eight, lose and your tournament is over, with no medal chance. That brings quarterfinal-level tension a round early.

At Paris 2024 the top four from each pool went straight through, so nothing like this has been played at the Games before. Carson Field's morning session offers up-close views of high-stakes hockey in an open-air South Bay setting.
HOC19.potentialContendersIntro: The play-in teams will not be known until the men's pool stage ends, so these names are speculative. They reflect recent form and the established teams most likely to be in the mix.

potentialContenders.name: Spain
potentialContenders.note: Runners-up at the 2026 World Cup, losing 1-0 to Germany in the final. They could land in the play-in if a pool goes badly.

potentialContenders.name: India
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists. A slip in pool play could send them into the play-in.

potentialContenders.name: Argentina
potentialContenders.note: 2026 World Cup bronze medalists. Tomas Domene was the top scorer in the 2025-26 Pro League with 21 goals.

potentialContenders.name: Australia
potentialContenders.note: Third in the 2025-26 Pro League and a two-time Pro League champion. They are a possible play-in team.

HOC20.blurb:
The second men's play-in session brings the other two knockout matches of the day. By night's end, four teams have reached the quarterfinals and four are heading home.

With pool play finished, the field is set by earlier results, and each team knows it has no margin left. Expect tense, cautious starts and late drama.

Carson Field's main pitch holds about 15,000 in temporary stands, with a smaller 5,000-seat secondary field on site. An evening session under the lights should suit a high-pressure, win-or-leave match.
HOC20.potentialContendersIntro: No one is confirmed for the play-in until pool results are in, so these are possible names. The 12-team field includes hosts the USA and qualifiers through March 2028.

potentialContenders.name: England
potentialContenders.note: Second in the 2025-26 Pro League behind Belgium. They are more likely to finish high in their pool, but could appear if results go against them.

potentialContenders.name: Spain
potentialContenders.note: 2026 World Cup runners-up and Paris 2024 fourth-place finishers. A possible play-in team if pool results are tight.

potentialContenders.name: India
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists and an established name. They could appear in a play-in match.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Qualify as hosts. They could land in the play-in and would bring a loud home crowd.

HOC21.blurb:
Hockey's new play-in round makes its debut on opening Sunday of the women's knockout phase. Every match is a straight knockout for a quarterfinal place.

Eight teams that miss the direct route from the pool stage play off for four quarterfinal spots. The format replaces Paris 2024, where the top four in each pool advanced automatically.

Expect a loud, fast session at Carson Field, a temporary hockey venue with about 15,000 seats. It sits beside the LA Galaxy's soccer stadium, so the park should be busy all day.
HOC21.potentialContendersIntro: The field is not set. Hosts USA and 2026 Asian Games champions India have qualified, but pool results will decide who plays in the play-in round. These teams are projections only.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host nation with an automatic place. Could land in the play-in round, depending on pool results.

potentialContenders.name: India
potentialContenders.note: Qualified as 2026 Asian Games champions after a 1-0 final win over China. Fifth at the 2026 World Cup, their best finish in 52 years.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: Likely contender if they qualify. They lost the 2026 World Cup fifth-place match to India.

potentialContenders.name: Japan
potentialContenders.note: Asian Games bronze medalists in 2026. Could appear if they qualify through the early-2028 tournaments.

HOC22.blurb:
This is the evening half of the women's play-in double. Two matches decide who joins the quarterfinals and who goes home.

Four of the eight play-in teams advance to Tuesday's quarterfinals. There is no second chance after a loss, so every penalty corner matters.

The second session runs into the night at Carson Field. Hockey on a temporary stadium pitch in Carson should feel intimate, with the stands close to the action.
HOC22.potentialContendersIntro: Only the USA, the Netherlands and India are confirmed so far. Four more places per gender come from early-2028 qualifiers, so the teams below are projections.

potentialContenders.name: China
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists. They lost the 2026 Asian Games final to India and must qualify another way; could appear if they do.

potentialContenders.name: Australia
potentialContenders.note: Fourth at the 2026 World Cup after losing both the semifinal and the bronze match by 1-0. A likely contender if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: Runners-up at the 2025 EuroHockey Championship. Projected to compete if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host-nation place guaranteed. Could play in the play-in round, depending on pool results.

HOC23.blurb:
The men's knockout rounds begin with two quarterfinals. Win and you are a game from the medal matches; lose and the tournament ends.

The teams that went straight through from the pool stage meet the four play-in winners from July 22. Anyone who just survived a play-in will be coming in with momentum and little rest.

The morning session at Carson Field has an all-day-hockey feel. The stands are temporary, so the sightlines should be tight around the pitch.
HOC23.potentialContendersIntro: Confirmed men's qualifiers so far are the USA, Belgium and India. The quarterfinal lineup is not known, so these teams are projections based on current form and rankings.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 World Cup, beating Spain 1-0, and lead the FIH rankings. Paris 2024 silver medalists, so a likely contender if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Belgium

potentialContenders.name: Australia

potentialContenders.name: India
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists and 2026 Asian Games champions, so already qualified.

HOC24.blurb:
Monday's evening quarterfinals bring the second pair of men's knockout matches. The two winners go through to Wednesday's semifinals.

The defending champions, the Netherlands, won Paris 2024 in a shoot-out against Germany, their first men's title since 2000. If they qualify, they will be hunting a repeat.

The evening session at Carson Field should have a night-game atmosphere. Floodlights and a crowd of up to 15,000 give the quarterfinals a big-match feel.
HOC24.potentialContendersIntro: The lineup is unconfirmed. These are likely contenders based on 2026 results and could change after pool play and qualification.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands

potentialContenders.name: Spain
potentialContenders.note: 2026 World Cup runners-up, their first final since 1998. They beat the Netherlands 4-3 in the semifinal.

potentialContenders.name: Argentina
potentialContenders.note: Beat the Netherlands 2-1 for bronze at the 2026 World Cup. Projected contender if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: India
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists. They qualified by winning the 2026 Asian Games, beating Malaysia 5-1.

HOC25.blurb:
The women's quarterfinals start with a morning pair. The field combines the pool-stage leaders with the four play-in winners.

The Netherlands won Paris 2024, but Argentina won the 2026 World Cup in a shoot-out. A new rivalry has opened up, and the winner of this tournament may have to get past one of them.

Carson Field offers a close, loud setting for knockout hockey. The morning session should run in comfortable Southern California sun.
HOC25.potentialContendersIntro: Only the USA, the Netherlands and India are confirmed women's qualifiers so far. The list below is a projection of likely contenders.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champions and 2025-26 Pro League winners. Beaten by Argentina in the 2026 World Cup final shoot-out.

potentialContenders.name: Argentina
potentialContenders.note: 2026 World Cup champions and Pro League runners-up. Could be a favorite if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Belgium

potentialContenders.name: India

HOC26.blurb:
The second women's quarterfinal session closes Tuesday with two knockout matches at night. Winners earn a semifinal place on Thursday.

This tournament could have a lot of history in it. China won silver in Paris, Argentina won the 2026 World Cup, and Belgium won a World Cup medal for the first time since 1978.

The evening session at Carson Field should be lively. Floodlit hockey and a packed temporary stand should carry plenty of noise.
HOC26.potentialContendersIntro: The matchups are not known. These teams are projections based on recent results, and several have yet to qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Belgium

potentialContenders.name: China

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host-nation place secured. Could reach the quarterfinals if they get through the pool stage or the play-in round.

The first men's semifinal is a short 9 AM start, with a place in the gold medal match at stake. A loss sends a team to the bronze match.

Germany won the 2026 World Cup and beat the Netherlands in the 2025 EuroHockey final shoot-out. Whoever reaches the semifinal will be facing the in-form side if the Germans qualify.

The morning light at Carson Field should make for a lively early crowd. This is a chance to see a medal-deciding match on a relaxed morning schedule.

HOC28.blurb:
The evening men's semifinal is the second of two on Wednesday, and it ends with a team into the gold medal match. Expect an intense night under the lights.

Belgium won the 2025-26 Pro League and are a big presence in the rankings. India, Paris 2024 bronze medalists, qualified as 2026 Asian Games champions and could challenge anyone.

Carson Field's evening atmosphere should be different from the morning session. Late kickoffs and a packed crowd could make for a loud setting.

HOC29.blurb:
The first women's semifinal is at 9 AM Thursday. The winner is one match from gold, and the loser plays for bronze.

The Netherlands are the defending champions, and Argentina are the reigning World Cup champions. If both get through, a semifinal between them would be a rematch of the 2026 final.

The morning session at Carson Field has a relaxed feel, with temporary stands just steps from the pitch. It is a chance to see medal-round hockey earlier in the day.

HOC30.blurb:
The evening women's semifinal is the last before the medal matches. One team moves to Saturday night's final, and the other plays for bronze.

The field could include teams with fresh storylines. Belgium won their first World Cup medal since 1978, and China are hoping to return after winning silver in Paris.

The night crowd at Carson Field, with up to 15,000 seats, should create a strong atmosphere. Knockout hockey under lights is a good ticket for fans who want a big-match feel.
HOC30.potentialContendersIntro: The semifinal field depends on qualification and the quarterfinals. The athletes below are projections, not confirmed participants.

HOC31.blurb:
The men's bronze medal match is the last chance for a medal for two teams that just lost semifinals. For many players, it is the last match of a long tournament.

India won Paris 2024 bronze by beating Spain, and Spain then reached the 2026 World Cup final. The loser of a semifinal who fights back could still take home a medal.

Carson Field in the late morning should be relaxed but passionate. Bronze matches often have a warm atmosphere because both sets of fans know a medal is on the line.

HOC32.blurb:
The men's gold medal match closes out the hockey programme on Friday night. It decides who succeeds the Netherlands as champions.

Germany won the 2026 World Cup, beating Spain 1-0, and lost Paris 2024 to the Dutch in a shoot-out. Belgium and others will want to challenge, but nothing is decided until the semifinals.

Carson Field at night should be the best seat in hockey. Expect floodlights, a sellout crowd and a long evening of tension, with a possible shoot-out.
HOC32.potentialContendersIntro: The finalists are unknown. These players are projections based on 2026 results and are not confirmed selections.

potentialContenders.name: Alexander Hendrickx

potentialContenders.name: Marc Miralles

HOC33.blurb:
The women's bronze medal match gives two semifinal losers a last chance to leave with a medal. It follows a day of rest before Saturday night's final.

Argentina won Paris 2024 bronze by beating Belgium in a shoot-out. Belgium then won 2026 World Cup bronze, so this match could carry a lot of bronze-medal experience.

Carson Field at midday should feel upbeat. The temporary stands, close to the pitch, tend to produce a loud mix of supporters in a bronze match.

HOC34.blurb:
The women's gold medal match is the final event of the hockey tournament, on Saturday night at Carson Field. One team leaves as the 2028 champion.

The Netherlands won five women's golds, including Paris 2024, but Argentina beat them in a shoot-out in the 2026 World Cup final. That result could shape this final's storyline if both qualify.

Expect a crowd of up to 15,000 under the lights and a long final that could end in a shoot-out. Ticket-holders get to see the final women's medal match of the programme.
HOC34.potentialContendersIntro: The finalists are not set. These athletes are projections from the 2026 World Cup and Pro League, not confirmed participants.

potentialContenders.name: Julieta Jankunas

JUD01.blurb:
Judo opens the 2028 Games with a full morning of mat-side action. Women's -48kg and men's -60kg, the two lightest classes, kick off the program in Hall 2.

These are elimination rounds, so expect quick, tactical bouts and early upsets. Only those who survive reach the evening repechage, semifinals and medal bouts, and the USA has a guaranteed host place in both categories.

The hall is an indoor exhibition space in the downtown cluster near L.A. Live, with temporary stands around the mats. It's a good, accessible way to see many athletes in one sitting.
JUD01.potentialContendersIntro: Natsumi Tsunoda of Japan won women's -48kg at Paris 2024, and the 2026 world champions in Baku are the names to watch. Who actually competes in 2028 is not yet known.

potentialContenders.name: Assunta Scutto

potentialContenders.name: Ahmad Yusifov
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 men's -60kg world title in Baku, coming from behind in the final.

potentialContenders.name: Ryuju Nagayama
potentialContenders.note: 2025 men's -60kg world champion and 2026 bronze medalist; projected contender if selected.

JUD02.blurb:
The first judo medals of the 2028 Games are decided here. Women's -48kg and men's -60kg finish in one evening block of repechage, semifinals, bronze bouts and finals.

The lightest classes tend to be fast and unpredictable. The men's -60kg world title has gone to a different athlete in each of 2024, 2025 and 2026, and the women's -48kg field is led by Japan and Italy.

The finals bring a louder, more focused crowd to the temporary stands around the mats. Each class awards two bronzes, so you'll see four medal bouts per weight class, plus the final.

Day two of judo brings men's -66kg and women's -52kg elimination rounds, and with them two of the sport's biggest names. This is the morning where the favorites start their runs.

Men's -66kg is loaded with Japanese talent, and the 2026 worlds included three different Japanese world champions since 2024. Women's -52kg has storylines of its own, including a comeback from a Paris 2024 champion.

Morning sessions have a relaxed, wander-in feel in Hall 2. Several mats run side by side, so you can catch a few bouts before the evening medal block.

Men's -66kg could see Abe chase a third straight Games title. In women's -52kg, a rematch between Uta Abe and Paris champion Diyora Keldiyorova is a storyline to watch.

The evening session in Hall 2 packs repechage, semifinals and finals into three hours. Expect a dense, noisy crowd around the mats and a steady run of ippon-or-bust bouts.

The -73kg title has changed hands every year from 2024 to 2026, so expect surprises. In women's -57kg, Paris 2024 champion Christa Deguchi gave Canada its first judo gold.

It's a good session for sampling many nations. Hall 2's temporary stands put you close to the mats, and early rounds often feature the heavy hitters on the opening bouts.

Hall 2's morning session is a relaxed way to see heavyweights and half-heavyweights up close. Schedules may still change, so check times before you go.

The judo program ends with a team event. Mixed team bronze and gold medal matches close the competition on Saturday evening, with men and women fighting for one shared result.

Japan is the team to beat on the world circuit. It beat Russia 4-1 in the 2026 world final in Baku for its eighth world team title, a year after Georgia won its first.

LAC01.blurb:
Lacrosse returns to the Summer Games as a medal sport for the first time since 1908, and this is the first day of play. Three men's round-robin games kick off the tournament at Exposition Park Stadium.

The men play Sixes: six per side on a smaller field, with shorter games and constant motion. Six teams are in the field, and the United States is in as host. The other five places are still to be decided.

Exposition Park Stadium is a steep, tight, soccer-built bowl beside the Coliseum, so even a midday crowd should feel close to the action. Being there for the opening day of a revived sport is the draw.

LAC02.blurb:
Women's lacrosse is played for medals at the Summer Games for the first time, and the first night is a historic one. Three round-robin games run under the lights at Exposition Park Stadium.

The U.S. women arrive as the team to beat, with a 16-game sixes winning streak reported as of October 2026. Canada beat them in the 2022 World Games final, and the U.S. won the 2025 rematch 16-8.

Evening sessions in this stadium usually mean a loud supporters' end and cooler air as the sun drops. For a first-ever women's medal tournament, the opening night should carry a real sense of occasion.

Day two of the men's round robin brings three more games, and the early results begin to shape the medal picture. With only six teams, every result carries weight.

Sixes rewards quick transitions, fast decisions and sharp goalkeeping. Shorter games mean an early deficit can be hard to erase.

This is a good midday entry point for newcomers: easy to follow, high in scoring and played in a close-in stadium. Expect a mix of lacrosse diehards and curious fans.

The women's round robin continues under the lights with three more games. The U.S. has dominated sixes so far, so the question is who can push it.

The Americans won 2025 World Games games by scores like 25-13, 32-8 and 24-10, then needed a one-goal finish against Canada in 2026. Canada looks like the nearest challenger.

On a weeknight in Exposition Park, the safe-standing supporters' end gives the stadium real noise. Even a lopsided game offers fast, high-scoring lacrosse.

Midweek brings the middle of the men's round robin, with three games and the standings taking shape. This session also carries one of the sport's biggest open questions.

The Haudenosaunee, who invented the game, are ranked fifth in men's sixes. The IOC has said they cannot compete as their own team, though U.S. and Canadian governments have asked for a change. As of November 2026, no decision timetable existed.

If they are cleared, expect the stadium atmosphere to be especially charged. Even without them, this is a good midday session with a crowd that knows its lacrosse.

Expect a tight stadium crowd and a clear sense of history. A medal game in a short, fast format can turn on one run.

potentialContenders.note: Was in the 2025 U.S. Sixes pool. Could be a key playmaker if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Zach Currier
potentialContenders.note: Game MVP in Canada's 25-14 Atlas Cup win over Haudenosaunee. Likely candidate for Canada if it qualifies.

LAC12.blurb:
This is the closing session of the lacrosse tournament, with the first-ever women's lacrosse medals at the Summer Games up for grabs. The bronze and gold games follow the round robin.

The U.S. beat Canada 16-8 at the 2025 World Games, and 15-14 in the 2026 Pan-American final. Canada won in 2022, so a rematch would carry history.

A late-night finish in the stadium should have a big, loud atmosphere. The field is not yet set, so other teams could change the story.
LAC12.potentialContendersIntro: The 2028 women's rosters and field are not set. These players are possible standouts if their teams qualify and reach the medal games.

potentialContenders.name: Marie McCool
potentialContenders.note: MVP of the 2025 World Games women's sixes tournament. Could star again if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Emma LoPinto
potentialContenders.note: Scored the winner with 38 seconds left in the 2026 Pan-American final. Could appear if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Nicole Perroni
potentialContenders.note: Scored four goals in the 2026 Pan-American final. A likely Canadian contender if she makes the roster.

potentialContenders.name: Mao Kawamura
potentialContenders.note: Goalkeeper and MVP of the 2026 Asia-Pacific title win. Could be a factor if Japan qualifies.

MPN01.blurb:
Modern pentathlon opens the 2028 Games program, and this women's semifinal is its first act. It is the sport's first return to the opening days since 1992.

Eighteen athletes work through direct-elimination fencing, the new 70m eight-obstacle head-to-head race that replaces riding, swimming, and then the laser run. The race is long, and the shooting is where a lead can vanish.

Valley Complex 2 is a temporary open-air venue in Sepulveda Basin park. The morning session is a relaxed way to see the new format before the final.
MPN01.potentialContendersIntro: Michelle Gulyás won Paris 2024 gold, but 2028 rosters are not set. The names below are projections based on 2026 World Championship form.

potentialContenders.name: Blanka Guzi
potentialContenders.note: World No.1 and 2026 world champion with 1,485 points. Projected to be among the favorites if she keeps her form.

potentialContenders.name: Farida Khalil
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion and 2026 world silver medalist at age 15. A likely contender if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Kerenza Bryson
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world bronze medalist who reached that final with the last qualifying spot. Could be a podium threat.

potentialContenders.name: Michelle Gulyás
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist with a world-record 1,461 points. She missed the 2025 and 2026 Worlds through injury, so her 2028 status is uncertain.

MPN02.blurb:
The men's semifinal gives the Valley a morning of fencing, obstacle racing, swimming and a running-and-shooting finish. Eighteen athletes compete, and the new obstacle leg can reshuffle the standings before the laser run.

Egypt arrives with momentum. At the 2026 Worlds, Mohamed El-Ashqar posted the fastest obstacle time in the semifinals, and Egypt took team silver.

Expect a loud morning in a temporary park venue. Compact sightlines make the laser run easy to follow, and other Valley Zone sports are nearby for a full day out.
MPN02.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gold went to Egypt's Ahmed El-Gendy, but 2028 entries are not confirmed. These are projections based on 2026 form and rankings.

potentialContenders.name: Matej Lukes
potentialContenders.note: World No.1 who won his 2026 world semifinal with 1,557 points. A projected favorite if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Mohamed El-Ashqar
potentialContenders.note: Fastest obstacle time (18.39s) in the 2026 world semifinals. Could be a strong contender.

potentialContenders.name: Moutaz Mohamed
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion who placed fourth at the 2026 Worlds. Likely to push for a 2028 place.

potentialContenders.name: Marvin Dogue
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 World Cup Final in Budapest. A dark horse if he qualifies.

MPN03.blurb:
This is the women's medal session. Fencing, obstacle and swimming set the starting gaps for a laser run in which the first athlete across the line wins.

The field has changed since Paris 2024. Blanka Guzi is the reigning world champion, Farida Khalil is a teenage rival, and Michelle Gulyás is working back from injury.

The final is only two hours long, so the action is compressed. Valley Complex 2 should be loudest as the leaders run and shoot, with the standings changing at each stage.
MPN03.potentialContendersIntro: Gulyás took Paris 2024 gold, ahead of Élodie Clouvel and Seong Seung-Min. The 2028 final field is not set, and the names below are projected from recent results.

potentialContenders.name: Blanka Guzi
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champion who took the lead late in the laser run. Projected to be a top medal contender.

potentialContenders.name: Farida Khalil
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion and 2026 world silver medalist. The generational rival of Gulyás and Guzi.

potentialContenders.name: Kerenza Bryson
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world bronze medalist. Could return to the podium if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Michelle Gulyás
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champion. She missed the last two Worlds through injury, so her 2028 appearance is not guaranteed.

potentialContenders.name: Jana Attia
potentialContenders.note: Set a 25.17s obstacle mark in the 2026 world final. Her speed there could matter if she is in the 2028 field.

MPN04.blurb:
The men's final closes the four-day modern pentathlon program, and the laser run decides the medals. The first athlete across the line takes gold, which makes the finish easy to follow.

The field is led by Czechia's Matej Lukes, who won the 2026 world title after a laser run comeback. Egypt, defending 2028 champion's nation after Ahmed El-Gendy's Paris 2024 gold, brings deep talent.

The session runs only two hours, so there is little downtime. Valley Complex 2 should have a big-finish feel, with fans packed close to the running loop.
MPN04.potentialContendersIntro: El-Gendy won Paris 2024 gold, with Taishu Sato and Giorgio Malan next. These 2028 contenders are projections from 2026 results.

potentialContenders.name: Matej Lukes
potentialContenders.note: World No.1 and 2026 world champion with 1,586 points. Ran the final's fastest laser run. A projected favorite.

potentialContenders.name: Egor Gromadskii
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world silver medalist, five seconds behind Lukes. His 2028 eligibility is not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Seo Chang-wan
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world bronze medalist with 1,576 points. Could be a podium threat if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Moutaz Mohamed
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion who placed fourth at the 2026 Worlds. Likely to contend if he makes the Egyptian team.

potentialContenders.name: Ahmed El-Gendy
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist with a world-record 1,555 points. His 2028 participation is not confirmed.

MTB01.blurb:
One race, one hour and a half, no second chances. The men's cross-country final is a mass start with no heats, so everything gets decided in a single lap-after-lap fight on a rugged hillside loop.

Tom Pidcock won in Tokyo and again in Paris 2024, where he fixed a puncture and still caught Victor Koretzky. He won the 2026 world title but plans to step back from mountain biking in 2027, so his 2028 plans remain a storyline.

The Industry Hills course is new, built into hilltop terrain in the San Gabriel Valley with drops, jumps and technical sections. Riders pass several times, so you can move around the loop and see the race shift from one vantage point to the next.
MTB01.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gold went to Tom Pidcock, with Victor Koretzky second and Alan Hatherly third. The 2028 field is not set, so these names are projections based on recent form.

potentialContenders.name: Tom Pidcock
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist and 2026 world champion. He has said he hopes to chase a third straight title, but he plans to step away from mountain biking in 2027, so his status is speculative.

potentialContenders.name: Luca Martin
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 World Cup overall in both cross-country and short track. A likely contender if he keeps his form.

potentialContenders.name: Alan Hatherly
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and world champion in 2024 and 2025. He punctured and finished 27th at the 2026 worlds, so he could be a bounce-back candidate.

potentialContenders.name: Christopher Blevins
potentialContenders.note: 2025 World Cup overall champion in cross-country and short track. He could be a home-soil favorite if healthy after a 2026 broken collarbone.

potentialContenders.name: Charlie Aldridge
potentialContenders.note: Runner-up to Pidcock at the 2026 worlds and winner of the 2026 World Cup finale at Lake Placid. A projected medal threat.

MTB02.blurb:
The women's cross-country final has a simple premise and a lot of drama: everyone starts together and the first rider across the line after about 90 minutes takes gold. There are no heats to hide in.

Paris 2024 gold went to Pauline Ferrand-Prévot, with Haley Batten taking silver for the U.S. and Jenny Rissveds bronze. Rissveds, Rio 2016 champion, won the 2026 World Cup overall, while Sina Frei took the 2026 world title.

The new Industry Hills loop winds over a hilltop in the San Gabriel Valley, with drops, jumps and technical sections. Spectators can follow riders to different points on the course, and a home crowd could be loud if Batten is in contention.
MTB02.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 medalists were Ferrand-Prévot, Batten and Rissveds. Who lines up in 2028 is not settled, so the names below are projections from recent results.

potentialContenders.name: Sina Frei
potentialContenders.note: Won her first elite world title in 2026 and the World Cup finale at Lake Placid. A projected top contender.

potentialContenders.name: Jenny Rissveds
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and 2025 world champion. She won the 2026 World Cup overall, the first Swede to do so, and is a likely medal threat.

potentialContenders.name: Haley Batten
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist who was 10th at the 2026 worlds. If she qualifies, she would race on home soil.

potentialContenders.name: Martina Berta
potentialContenders.note: Runner-up at the 2026 worlds and second in a sprint finish at the Lake Placid World Cup finale. Could be a podium threat.

potentialContenders.name: Pauline Ferrand-Prévot
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist. She has returned to road racing and called 2028 an exciting goal, though one report says that target is on the road, so her mountain bike participation is uncertain.

OWS01.blurb:
The women's 10km opens open water swimming at the 2028 Games, and it will crown a brand-new champion. Paris 2024 winner Sharon van Rouwendaal announced her retirement in September 2025.

Twenty-two swimmers will start together in a single mass-start race inside the Long Beach Breakwater, with a maximum of two per nation. Australia's Moesha Johnson, the 2025 world champion, has dominated recent form, including a 2026 Pan Pacific win off Long Beach.

Belmont Shore is a natural beachfront set up with temporary facilities. Fans can watch from the shoreline and around Belmont Veterans Memorial Pier as the pack churns just offshore for roughly two hours.
OWS01.potentialContendersIntro: The Paris 2024 podium is partly intact, but van Rouwendaal has retired. Entries for 2028 are unconfirmed, so these are projections based on 2025-2026 form.

potentialContenders.name: Moesha Johnson
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist and 2025 world 10km champion. Won the 2026 Pan Pacs off Long Beach and swept the 2026 World Cup 10km races. Projected favorite if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Ginevra Taddeucci
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and 2026 European 10km champion. Took silver behind Johnson at the 2025 Worlds. Likely contender, though not yet qualified.

potentialContenders.name: Airi Ebina
potentialContenders.note: Finished second to Johnson at the 2026 Pan Pacs in Long Beach and in Cancun in November 2026. Could emerge as a medal threat if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Ichika Kajimoto
potentialContenders.note: Ranked No. 2 in the world entering the 2026 Pan Pacs and placed third in that Long Beach race. A projected contender if she makes the field.

potentialContenders.name: Lisa Pou
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world 10km bronze medalist. A possible podium threat if she qualifies and returns to form.

OWS02.blurb:
The men's 10km closes out the open water program with a one-day-later echo of the women's race. Paris 2024 champion Kristof Rasovszky of Hungary could return, but the current form line runs through Germany's Florian Wellbrock.

As in the women's race, 22 swimmers share a single mass start inside the Long Beach Breakwater, with no more than two per nation. Packs, drafting and a late sprint often decide medals, as seen in recent Wellbrock wins.

Expect a beachfront crowd along Belmont Shore and the area near Belmont Veterans Memorial Pier. The swimmers stay close to land, which makes the finish easy to follow from the sand.
OWS02.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gold went to Rasovszky, silver to Oliver Klemet and bronze to David Betlehem. None of the names below has confirmed a 2028 entry, so these are projections from recent form.

potentialContenders.name: Florian Wellbrock
potentialContenders.note: Tokyo 2020 10km champion and 2025 world champion. Won the 2026 European title and the 2026 Pan Pacs off Long Beach, and ranked No. 1 in the world in August 2026. Projected favorite if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: David Betlehem
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and 2026 World Cup overall leader. Took silver at the 2026 Europeans. A likely podium contender if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Gregorio Paltrinieri
potentialContenders.note: Silver medalist at the 2025 Worlds who prioritized open water in 2026. A veteran who could factor in if he competes and qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Oliver Klemet
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist who placed third at the 2026 Europeans. Germany could send two swimmers, so he is a possible entrant.

potentialContenders.name: Kristof Rasovszky
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist. He finished 23rd at the 2026 Europeans, so his 2028 form is an open question.

RCB01.blurb:
Coastal rowing makes its Games debut on the Long Beach shoreline, and this opening morning is where the solo fields get sorted. Two time trials set the seeding, then the last 16 begins head-to-head knockout racing.

Each race is a sprint across the sand, a 250m slalom row through the surf around two buoys, a 180-degree turn, and a run back up the beach. It is the first time a Games rowing event is raced on open ocean.

Seeding helps but doesn't decide much. At the 2026 world finals, Samuel Forbes was seventh in the time trials and still won men's solo silver. Rough surf and capsizes marked those trials.

Fans watch from the Belmont Shore waterfront near the pier, with the action just offshore. Expect an early-morning, beach-day atmosphere as quota-earning nations, one man and one woman each, take their first strokes.
RCB01.potentialContendersIntro: Nobody is confirmed for 2028, since places are decided mainly at the October 2027 world finals in Oeiras. These names come from recent world finals form and are projections only.

potentialContenders.name: Moritz Wolff
potentialContenders.note: Fastest men's solo time trial at the 2026 world finals, 3.3 seconds ahead of Chris Bak, and bronze medalist there. A likely time-trial threat if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Chris Bak
potentialContenders.note: Men's solo world champion in 2024 and 2025 and second fastest in the 2026 time trial. Could appear if he earns a US place.

potentialContenders.name: Isabella Scammell
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 women's solo time trial by seven seconds and went on to take the world title. A projected front-runner if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Magdalena Lobnig
potentialContenders.note: Women's solo world champion in 2024 and a medalist three years running through 2026. Could contend if she qualifies for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Raminta Morkunaite
potentialContenders.note: Second in the 2026 women's solo time trial 1. A possible seeding contender if Lithuania qualifies her.

RCB02.blurb:
Two medal finals, back to back, as the first coastal rowing champions in Games history are decided. Women's and men's solo Final 8 races turn a beach run, a surf launch and a buoy turn into a knockout sprint.

Each race is about 250m out through the surf and back, bookended by sprints across the sand. One capsize, a missed buzzer or a wrong turn at a buoy can end a medal bid, as several favorites found at the 2026 world finals.

Chris Bak (USA) is the most decorated beach sprinter so far, but 2026 showed the field catching up. None of these athletes is confirmed for 2028, since places are decided mainly at the 2027 worlds in Portugal.

At Belmont Shore, fans watch from the shoreline near Belmont Veterans Memorial Pier while the races run just offshore. Expect a beach-party feel, with the finish line only steps from the crowd.
RCB02.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected contenders based on recent world finals results; none is confirmed for 2028. The list covers the men's and women's solo events.

potentialContenders.name: Chris Bak

potentialContenders.name: Liu Jiayu

potentialContenders.name: Samuel Forbes
potentialContenders.note: 2026 men's solo silver medallist at age 20, who knocked out Bak in the quarterfinals. Could be a rising threat.

potentialContenders.name: Isabella Scammell

potentialContenders.name: Magdalena Lobnig
potentialContenders.note: Women's solo gold in 2024, silver in 2025 and bronze in 2026. Podium regular, though not confirmed for 2028.

RCB03.blurb:
The first mixed-gender rowing event ever held at the Games begins here. Mixed double sculls crews race two time trials to set the seeding, then go head-to-head in the last 16.

A man and a woman share the boat, and the beach sprint format demands both a fast run and clean handling through the surf. The 2026 world finals showed how fragile a campaign can be: Germany's eventual champions nearly went out the day before their final.

This is an accessible early-round session, good for catching a wide field of nations. Crews can be changed from those who earned the quota place, so line-ups remain uncertain.

Spectators line the sand at Belmont Shore for a morning of fast, short races. With so many crews on the water, there is plenty of action between the time trials and the knockouts.
RCB03.potentialContendersIntro: Projected crews are based on recent world finals; none is confirmed for 2028, and nations may swap athletes. Names below are for the mixed double sculls.

potentialContenders.name: Dominykas Jancionis and Martyna Kazlauskaite
potentialContenders.note: Won mixed double world gold in 2024 and 2025 and took 2026 silver. Likely contenders if they stay together.

potentialContenders.name: Franz Werner and Sophie Leupold
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champions, Germany's first open beach sprint world title. Could return, though Germany has shown it will reshuffle crews.

potentialContenders.name: Isabella Scammell and Oscar Scheel Gambo
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 mixed double time trial. Australia is a rising beach sprint nation.

potentialContenders.name: Su Juntao and Liu Lili
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 Youth Games mixed double and the under-19 world title. Possible senior threats in the coming years.

potentialContenders.name: Ander Martin and Esther Briz Zamorano

RCB04.blurb:
History gets made on the water: the first Games medals ever awarded in a mixed-gender rowing event. The mixed double sculls Final 8 decides gold, silver and bronze in a short, chaotic sprint.

Each crew runs to the boat, rows through the surf to the buoy and back, then sprints up the beach. At the 2026 worlds, Germany beat two-time champions Lithuania in the finish sprint, and the margins are often tiny.

The field is wide open. Lithuania, Germany, Spain, the USA and a fast-improving China all have recent podium form, but crews for 2028 will not be set until after the October 2027 worlds in Oeiras.

At Belmont Shore, fans crowd the beach near Belmont Veterans Memorial Pier with the finish line right in front of them. Expect a loud, close-up medal finale with the Pacific as the backdrop.
RCB04.potentialContendersIntro: None of these crews is confirmed for 2028, so this is a projection from recent world finals. Pairings could change before the Games.

potentialContenders.name: Franz Werner and Sophie Leupold
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champions who beat Lithuania in the finish sprint. Could defend their form if they qualify together.

potentialContenders.name: Dominykas Jancionis and Martyna Kazlauskaite
potentialContenders.note: Gold in 2024 and 2025, then 2026 silver. Likely medal contenders if they remain a crew.

potentialContenders.name: Ander Martin

potentialContenders.name: Chris Bak

potentialContenders.name: Su Juntao and Liu Lili
potentialContenders.note: 2026 Youth Games champions. A speculative rising threat if they graduate to senior level.

ROW01.blurb:
The regatta opens on Marine Stadium's narrow saltwater channel, with the women's single sculls heats and the men's double sculls and pair heats. Everyone starts here, and no medals are decided yet.

All three events race a historically short 1,500 metres, the shortest course ever used at the Games. Lane draws and quick starts matter more over less distance, and heats put plenty of pressure on early positioning.

The 2025 world champion, Fiona Murtagh of Ireland, is a likely name to watch in the women's single, if she qualifies. Paris 2024 gold went to Karolien Florijn (NED), ahead of Emma Twigg (NZL) and Viktorija Senkutė (LTU).

Spectators watch from the shoreline beside the racing lanes, with Belmont Shore and the Long Beach skyline behind. It is a relaxed late-afternoon introduction to a venue that first hosted Games rowing in 1932.
ROW01.potentialContendersIntro: These contenders are for the women's single sculls heats. Fiona Murtagh won the 2025 world title in Shanghai, but 2028 fields will not be set until qualification wraps up after the 2027 worlds in Lucerne.

potentialContenders.name: Fiona Murtagh
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion in the women's single sculls (7:12.27 in Shanghai). A likely top seed if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Karolien Florijn

potentialContenders.name: Lauren Henry
potentialContenders.note: Silver medalist at the 2025 world championships. A projected medal threat if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Frida Sanggaard Nielsen
potentialContenders.note: Bronze medalist at the 2025 worlds. A likely finalist if she makes the field.

ROW02.blurb:
Sunday morning brings the men's single sculls heats, the first look at one of rowing's deepest events. The men's double sculls and pair also race semifinals, and the women's double sculls and pair run heats.

The single field is the main draw. Oliver Zeidler (GER) won Paris 2024, Stefanos Ntouskos (GRE) took the 2025 world title, and Zeidler won another world title in 2026, so a Zeidler-Ntouskos rematch looks possible if both qualify.

The men's double and pair semifinals are where finalists are sorted from the rest. Missing the A final over 1,500 metres leaves little room to recover.

Expect a morning crowd on the shoreline with the sun climbing over the Alamitos Bay channel. With five events racing in under two hours, the session moves fast.
ROW02.potentialContendersIntro: These contenders are for the men's single sculls heats and the men's double sculls semifinals. Paris 2024 medalists and recent world champions are the natural starting point, though 2028 qualification is still ahead.

potentialContenders.name: Oliver Zeidler
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist in the men's single sculls, and a 2026 world champion. A projected favorite if he competes.

potentialContenders.name: Stefanos Ntouskos
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion in the men's single sculls (6:36.75). A likely contender if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Yauheni Zalaty
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist, competing as an Individual Neutral Athlete. His 2028 eligibility and status are not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Simon van Dorp
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 single sculls bronze medalist and 2026 world champion in the men's double sculls. Could appear in the double semifinals.

ROW03.blurb:
The first medals of the regatta are decided Monday morning, with the men's double sculls and men's pair A, B and C finals. The women's single sculls quarterfinals and the women's double and pair semifinals share the program.

Paris 2024 gold went to Romania in the men's double, with the Netherlands taking silver, and to Croatia in the men's pair. Simon van Dorp (NED) won the 2026 world double sculls title, so the Dutch could be a medal threat again.

In the women's single quarterfinals, the 2025 world champion Fiona Murtagh (IRL) could appear, along with Karolien Florijn (NED), who won Paris 2024.

The finals are short, loud and close to the bank. At Marine Stadium, where 1932 crews once raced four abreast, spectators can watch a medal race from a few steps away.
ROW03.potentialContendersIntro: These contenders are for the men's double sculls final and the women's single sculls quarterfinals. All 2028 participation is projected until qualification ends.

potentialContenders.name: Simon van Dorp
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champion in the men's double sculls and the mixed double sculls. A likely contender in the double if he stays in that boat.

potentialContenders.name: Fiona Murtagh
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion in the women's single sculls. Likely to appear in the quarterfinals if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Karolien Florijn
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist in the women's single sculls. Her 2028 plans are not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Lauren Henry
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world silver medalist in the women's single sculls. A projected quarterfinal threat if she qualifies.

ROW04.blurb:
Tuesday's medal action is in the women's double sculls and women's pair, with A, B and C finals. The session also includes the men's quadruple sculls and four heats and the men's single sculls quarterfinals.

Paris 2024 gave New Zealand gold in the women's double, with Romania second, and the Netherlands gold in the women's pair, again with Romania second. At the 2026 worlds, the United States took pair bronze and a world best time was set in the pair.

The men's four heats are worth watching for the United States, which won Paris 2024 and the 2026 world title. The single sculls quarterfinals could bring Oliver Zeidler (GER) or Stefanos Ntouskos (GRE) back on the water.

Morning racing at Marine Stadium is easy to follow, with finals in close sequence and the course alongside the bank. It is a good day to catch both medal races and heats.
ROW04.potentialContendersIntro: These crews are for the women's double sculls and pair finals, based on Paris 2024 and the 2026 worlds. Actual 2028 crews and rosters are not set.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands women's pair
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists in the women's pair. A projected contender if the Dutch field a strong crew.

potentialContenders.name: Romania women's pair
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists in the women's pair. A likely medal threat if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: United States women's pair
potentialContenders.note: Bronze medalists at the 2026 worlds, where a world best time was set in the event. A possible contender.

potentialContenders.name: New Zealand women's double
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists in the women's double sculls. Whether they return as a crew is unknown.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands women's double
potentialContenders.note: Roos de Jong won silver in the event at the 2026 worlds. A possible Dutch medal contender.

ROW05.blurb:
Wednesday's marquee races are the men's quadruple sculls and men's four A and B finals. The women's quadruple sculls and four heats and the women's single sculls semifinals also run.

The Netherlands won the Paris 2024 men's quad, and the United States won the men's four at Paris and again at the 2026 worlds. Germany won a 2026 worlds quad heat in 6:16.11, ahead of Australia and Poland.

The women's four heats include the United States, whose crew won the 2026 world title in a world best 6:09.87. The single sculls semifinals also show who might be a title favorite, with Fiona Murtagh (IRL) the 2025 world champion.

A four or quad racing over 1,500 metres should be loud and close along the Marine Stadium bank. This is a good day to see crew boats with real medal stakes.
ROW05.potentialContendersIntro: These crews are for the men's quadruple sculls and men's four finals. They come from Paris 2024 and world championship results. 2028 crews are still projected.

potentialContenders.name: United States men's four
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists and 2026 world champions. A projected favorite if the crew stays strong.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands men's quadruple sculls
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists. A likely contender if they keep their level.

potentialContenders.name: Germany men's quadruple sculls
potentialContenders.note: Won a 2026 worlds heat in 6:16.11. A possible medal threat in the quad.

ROW06.blurb:
Thursday's medal races are the women's quadruple sculls and women's four A and B finals. The men's eight heats open the big-boat program, and the men's single sculls semifinals and E and F finals fill out the morning.

Great Britain won the Paris 2024 women's quad, with the Netherlands second, and the Dutch won the women's four. The United States won the 2026 world title in the four in a world best 6:09.87 and took quad bronze.

The men's eight heats matter because the Netherlands won the 2025 world title ahead of Great Britain and the United States. Each crew is trying to avoid the repechage and keep a direct path to the final.

The finals are a clean, quick watch from the bank. A 9:30 start leaves time for the full session before the day warms up.

ROW07.blurb:
Friday brings the men's eight A and B finals, the biggest boat on the Marine Stadium course. The session also has the women's eight heats and the women's single sculls A to D finals.

The Netherlands won the 2025 and 2026 world titles, with Finn Florijn, Wibout Rustenburg and Jonna de Vries among the crew. Great Britain won Paris 2024 with the Dutch second, and the 2025 worlds had Great Britain second and the United States third.

The women's single A final could bring in Fiona Murtagh (IRL), the 2025 world champion, and Karolien Florijn (NED), the Paris 2024 gold medalist, if they qualify. The shorter 1,500 metres may help crews with fast starts.

Eights are the loudest races on the bank, with eight rowers and a coxswain flashing by in seconds. A 10:00 AM start fits a full session before lunch.

ROW08.blurb:
The regatta ends Saturday with the men's single sculls A to D finals and the women's eight A and B finals. It is a short final session, with the last medals on Marine Stadium.

Oliver Zeidler (GER) won Paris 2024, Stefanos Ntouskos (GRE) won the 2025 worlds with Zeidler second, and Zeidler won again in 2026. Yauheni Zalaty (AIN) was Paris silver, and Simon van Dorp (NED) was bronze.

In the women's eight, Romania won Paris 2024 and the 2026 world title, and the United States took 2026 worlds bronze. If those crews hold, it could be a Romania-United States final.

The finale gives a single in the morning light and a big eight on the bank. With Belmont Shore and the Long Beach skyline behind, it is a fitting close to a regatta that began here in 1932.

RU701.blurb:
The 2028 rugby sevens tournament starts with a Wednesday morning triple-header of women's pool matches. Six games in three hours means the pitch is rarely empty.

The 12-team field is not set. The United States is in as host, and the rest will come through the 2027 SVNS standings, regional qualifiers and a June 2028 repechage.

Carson Stadium is a soccer-specific bowl of about 27,000 seats, so even a pool match feels close to the action. Expect a lively early crowd and a first look at the field.

The evening pool session is where the host crowd can show up in force. Six matches run from 4 to 7 PM on opening day.

The USA qualified automatically as host and arrives as the Paris 2024 bronze medalist. Ilona Maher, 30, has said she is returning to rugby and working toward selection, though nothing is guaranteed.

South Bay sun and evening light on an open-air pitch make a good setting for the women's game, and every seat sits close to the field.

Pool play ends Thursday morning, and the standings decide who gets Thursday afternoon's quarterfinals. Teams that miss out drop into the 9-12 classification bracket.

By the end of the three hours, the eight quarterfinalists are set. The final pool games can swing on point differential, so scoreboards matter all session.

It is a good morning to scout the field at Carson Stadium. You can see how the teams are shaping up before the knockout rounds begin.

Thursday evening is where the women's tournament turns to win-or-go-home. Four quarterfinals decide who plays for medals, and the 9-12 classification matches run alongside.

Winners advance to Saturday's semifinals. Losers drop to the 5-8 bracket and lose their medal chance. Sevens is fast, and one error can end a run.

With 27,000 seats and clear sight lines, Carson Stadium should feel loud for a host-nation quarterfinal if the USA is in one.

Saturday afternoon has the two women's semifinals, with gold and bronze matches coming that evening. Alongside them are the 5-8 classification and 9-12 placing games.

Semifinal winners play for gold and losers for bronze. In Paris, New Zealand and Canada won their semifinals, and the USA lost before taking bronze.

The session also gives the crowd a real chance to see 5-8 and 9-12 matches, which still carry national pride and seeding value.

The first rugby sevens medals of the 2028 Games are decided here. Saturday night brings the 5-8 placing matches, the bronze match and the gold medal match.

New Zealand is chasing a third straight women's title after Tokyo and Paris 2024. Australia, the first champion at Rio 2016, beat New Zealand 26-19 in the 2026 World Championship final.

New Zealand and Australia met in all six 2025/26 regular-season finals, and New Zealand rallied from 21-5 down to win in New York. A final at Carson Stadium under the lights could be tense.

France enters as Paris 2024 champion after beating Fiji 28-7. The USA is in as host, and the other teams will come through SVNS standings, regional qualifiers and the June 2028 repechage.

A Sunday-morning start gives you a relaxed, family-friendly look at the sport at Carson Stadium, where nearly every seat is close to the touchline.

Sunday evening brings the second block of men's pool play, six more matches. The defending champions are likely to be in the mix.

France won in Paris, and Antoine Dupont came off the bench in the final to score two tries. He has said a sevens return appeals to him, but only after the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

Fiji, under coach Osea Kolinisau through 2028, will look to bounce back from that final loss. Pool games here are a fast, easy way to see the field.

Point differential and bonus margins can matter, so late scores can change the picture. A team with a loss can still advance, and a pool leader is not safe until the last whistle.

It is a showdown morning for anyone who likes pool-play drama. The USA won its pool at Bordeaux 2026 before finishing fifth, so a home pool run is plausible.
