SAL01.blurb:
Sailing opens at Belmont Shore with the first day of the kite qualification series. Foiling kiteboarders sprint around short courses just offshore, with the first Games sailing medals only days away.

Qualifying sorts the fleet ahead of the July 19 finals. Max Maeder of Singapore won the 2026 world title, and France's Lauriane Nolot took the women's crown, so both arrive as form leaders if they qualify.

The course sits close to the beach, so fans on the sand and near Belmont Veterans Memorial Pier can follow the action. Long Beach also hosted sailing at the 1984 Los Angeles Games, which adds some history to the setting.

The windsurfers also race on new equipment. Men have moved to 8 sq m sails and women to a newly designed 7.3 sq m sail, so the 2028 Games will be the first to use them.

With two fleets sharing the course area, there is plenty to watch from the shoreline. Races run just offshore, and you can follow the foils and kites from the beach and the pier area.

For the windsurfers, the series is a long test of consistency on foils. The 2026 Worlds were tight, with Israel and the Netherlands both strong and several former champions chasing form.

This is an accessible entry point for fans who want to see the sport without the pressure of a medal race. The racing stays close to shore at Belmont Shore, which makes it easy to follow from the beach.

The kite finals share the day with the final windsurfing qualifying races. That gives fans two disciplines in one session, with the windsurfing medals the next day.

The 2026 Worlds showed how fast kite fortunes can change. Max Maeder won his third world title, and Jessie Kampman crashed in the women's final as Lauriane Nolot took the crown.

Because the kite courses run close to the beach, fans on the shoreline and near the pier get a close view of the racing.

At the 2026 Worlds, the Grand Final went to the first rider to reach two match points. The same pressure should apply to the medal races, and the session is short, only three hours.

Fans on the shoreline and near the pier can follow the finals from the beach as the foilers race close to shore.

The sailing programme at the Port of Los Angeles begins here, with the men's and women's one-person dinghy fleets starting their qualification series. Nobody wins a medal today, but the standings start to take shape.

The ILCA 7 and ILCA 6 are single-handed boats, so every result comes down to one sailor's tactics, fitness and nerve. Fleet racing means a single bad start can cost real points.

The harbor sits in San Pedro Bay, the same waters that hosted the 1932 regatta. Spectators watch from shore with working container-port cranes and ships behind the racecourse, a backdrop few regattas offer.

SAL07.blurb:
Day two widens the field. The one-person dinghies continue their qualification series, while the mixed two-person dinghy (470) and mixed multihull (Nacra 17) fleets start racing for the first time.

The Nacra 17 is the one to watch for spectacle. At the 2025 worlds, medal races were sailed on foiling catamarans at more than 20 knots in rough seas.

The 470 is a very different test, with a helm and crew working in tight sync. Both mixed events are open and unsettled: Britain's Gimson and Burnet won the 2025 Nacra 17 title, but a first-time champion took the 2026 crown.

From the shoreline, the harbor course keeps boats close enough to follow the starts and mark roundings without binoculars.

SAL08.blurb:
The skiffs arrive. The men's 49er and women's 49erFX open their series today, joining the ongoing dinghy, mixed dinghy and multihull racing for the busiest day of the prelim stretch so far.

Skiffs are fast, twitchy and physically demanding, with two-person crews trapezing off the wing in the breeze. Capsizes and big comebacks are part of the show.

The men's skiff has a clear storyline. Spain won Paris 2024 gold, New Zealand took silver and the United States took bronze, and the Spanish crew won the 2025 world title while the Kiwis took 2026.

Four classes racing in one afternoon give the harbor a lively feel, with plenty of boats to watch.
SAL08.potentialContendersIntro: These contenders are for the opening days of the men's 49er and women's 49erFX. They are projections from recent worlds results, not confirmed 2028 entries.

potentialContenders.name: Pia Dahl Andersen / Nora Edland
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 49erFX Worlds, winning the final race to take the title. Could be a threat if they qualify.

SAL09.blurb:
This is the first medal day of the dinghy classes. The men's and women's one-person dinghy finals decide gold, silver and bronze, with skiffs on day two and the mixed boats on day three.

Both ILCA fields have been unpredictable lately. The men's world title changed hands in 2025 and 2026, and the 2026 worlds were decided under sailing's new finals format.

Home interest could run high in the women's fleet. American Charlotte Rose won the 2026 ILCA 6 Worlds, which would make her a contender if she qualifies.

Be in the harbor early. Medal racing is where tactical duels play out in the open, and the shoreline gives a close view of the finish.
SAL09.potentialContendersIntro: Contenders are for the men's ILCA 7 and women's ILCA 6 finals. Matt Wearn and Marit Bouwmeester won at Paris 2024, but 2028 participation is not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Willem Wiersema

potentialContenders.name: Marit Bouwmeester
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 women's one-person dinghy gold medalist. Only a contender if she continues competing toward 2028.

SAL10.blurb:
Two more golds go on the line today. The mixed two-person dinghy (470) and mixed multihull (Nacra 17) hold their finals, while the skiffs race their third day.

The Nacra 17 final is the highlight, with foiling catamarans lifting out of the water at high speed. Italy won at Paris 2024, but Britain's Gimson and Burnet won the 2025 world title and the class has since crowned a new champion.

The 470 offers a contrast. Austria won Paris 2024 gold, and Spain's Xammar and Cardona overtook a leading British pair on the final leg to win the 2025 worlds.

With medals on the water and the skiffs still racing, it is a full late afternoon of action in San Pedro Bay.
SAL10.potentialContendersIntro: Contenders are for the mixed Nacra 17 and mixed 470 finals. These are projections from recent form, since 2028 crews are not confirmed.

potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 Nacra 17 Worlds, their third title in the class, and took bronze in 2026. Likely contenders if they stay together.

potentialContenders.name: Gianluigi Ugolini / Maria Giubilei
potentialContenders.note: Runners-up to Gimson and Burnet at the 2025 Worlds. Italy won Nacra 17 gold at Paris 2024.

potentialContenders.note: Fourth at the 2025 Nacra 17 Worlds, their best result. Could challenge for a medal.

potentialContenders.name: Jordi Xammar / Marta Cardona
potentialContenders.note: 2025 mixed 470 world champions. Projected medal contenders if they compete.

potentialContenders.name: Martin Wrigley / Bettine Harris
potentialContenders.note: Third at the 2025 470 Worlds after leading most of the final race. A potential podium threat.

SAL11.blurb:
The sailing finale. The men's skiff (49er) and women's skiff (49erFX) medals are the last decided in sailing, closing the regatta on July 28 at the Port of Los Angeles.

The skiffs are the fastest, most athletic boats in the regatta, and a final can swing on one gust or one capsize. The shorter 2:00-5:00 PM window is built around the climax.

The men's field looks open. Spain won Paris 2024 gold, New Zealand silver and the United States bronze, and Spain's Botín and Trittel won the 2025 world title. The Kiwi pair of Menzies and Lee Rush won in 2026.

It is a good ticket for fans who want a medal outcome in a harbor setting, with the last finishes close to shore.
SAL11.potentialContendersIntro: Contenders are for the men's 49er and women's 49erFX finals. They are projections from recent world championship results, not confirmed 2028 crews.

potentialContenders.name: Seb Menzies / George Lee Rush
potentialContenders.note: 2026 49er world champions after a close final race. Menzies also co-helms Emirates Team New Zealand's America's Cup boats.

potentialContenders.name: Bart Lambriex / Floris van de Werken

potentialContenders.name: Paula Barceló / María Cantero

potentialContenders.name: Pia Dahl Andersen / Nora Edland
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 49erFX Worlds by one point, taking the final race. Could be a threat if they qualify.

SHO01.blurb:
Two air rifle titles are decided in one long Saturday session. Qualification comes first, then the men's and women's finals. Each final strips a field of eight down to a single winner by elimination.

The Doha world championships in November 2026 put China's Sheng Lihao (men) and South Korea's Ban Hyojin (women) back on top. Both are Paris 2024 champions, and neither spot at the 2028 Games is guaranteed.

The temporary range sits inside the Long Beach Convention Center on the downtown waterfront. It is a quiet, hushed setting where a single shot can swing a medal, and the beach volleyball, aquatics and climbing venues are a short walk away.
SHO01.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 champions Sheng Lihao and Ban Hyojin both won world titles in Doha in 2026. Their 2028 participation is projected, not confirmed, and Chinese teammates are strong in both events.

potentialContenders.name: Sheng Lihao

potentialContenders.name: Zhang Changhong
potentialContenders.note: Fourth in the Doha men's final and a 2026 World Cup winner in Munich. Could challenge his teammates for China's place.

potentialContenders.note: Silver medalist in Doha (252.2), just behind Ban. Could be a medal threat if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Maximilian Dallinger
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion in Cairo (252). Projected to be in the men's mix if he qualifies for Germany.

SHO02.blurb:
Air pistol takes over the hall on Sunday, with the men's and women's events both going from qualification to finals. It is a precision contest of tiny margins, where one shot out of the ten-ring can decide a medal.

China has been the force lately. Hu Kai and Jiang Ranxin won the 2026 world titles in Doha, and Paris 2024 champion Xie Yu was part of China's winning team.

India's Manu Bhaker, a Paris 2024 bronze medalist, was fifth in Doha and missed a quota place there. Fans in Long Beach can watch the lanes up close in an indoor range inside the convention center.
SHO02.potentialContendersIntro: China won both 2026 world titles in Doha, but 2028 rosters are not set. Paris 2024 medalists such as Xie Yu, Oh Ye-Jin and Manu Bhaker could return if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Hu Kai

potentialContenders.name: Xie Yu
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 men's champion and part of China's 2026 world team title. Could appear if he earns a place.

potentialContenders.name: Jiang Ranxin
potentialContenders.note: 2026 women's world champion (242.4), just ahead of teammate Yao Qianxun. A likely medal threat if she competes.

potentialContenders.name: Oh Ye-Jin

potentialContenders.name: Manu Bhaker
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist who finished fifth in Doha. Could come back if India fields her, but no quota was earned there.

SHO03.blurb:
Skeet's opening day is where the 2028 shotgun story begins, as men and women start qualification at Whittier Narrows. No medals are awarded today, but a few missed targets can end a final run before it starts.

Under the 2026 rulebook the top eight from qualification reach the final, up from six at Paris 2024. Qualification continues on day 2, so day 1 scores set the pace.

This is an open-air range in the San Gabriel Valley parkland. Temporary stands behind the stations are planned to seat about 2,000, and fans watch clays fly out over green fields. Expect hushed concentration between shots and applause for perfect rounds.
SHO03.potentialContendersIntro: Day 1 covers both men's and women's skeet. Paris 2024 results are confirmed, but 2028 rosters are not, so the names below are projections based on recent form.

potentialContenders.name: Vincent Hancock
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 men's skeet champion and reigning world champion. He has said he intends to go for a fifth gold and set a 36 final world record at Lonato in 2026. His place on the U.S. team is not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Jesper Hansen
potentialContenders.note: Tied for the lead with a perfect 50 after day 1 at the 2026 World Championship in Doha. He went on to win the world title. Denmark has already secured a men's quota place.

potentialContenders.name: Samantha Simonton
potentialContenders.note: 2025 women's skeet world champion and winner of the 2026 USA Shooting Fall Skeet Selection Match. A likely contender for a U.S. spot.

potentialContenders.name: Francisca Crovetto
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 women's skeet champion. Whether she is in the 2028 field depends on qualification.

potentialContenders.name: Jiang Yiting
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 women's skeet world title in Doha. China swept that podium, so she is a projected medal threat if selected.

SHO04.blurb:
The mixed team events have a new look for 2028. The top four qualifying teams go into one medal final using elimination, with no separate gold and bronze matches. The session covers both rifle and pistol.

The format was tried at the 2026 world championships in Doha. China won the rifle title and Shen Yiyao and Bu Shuaihang took the pistol title, while South Korea settled for rifle bronze by 0.8 points.

Expect a tense evening in the Long Beach hall, with the crowd leaning in as each team is eliminated. Medals are decided in a single final rather than in separate matches.
SHO04.potentialContendersIntro: Contenders below are projected from Doha 2026 results for the rifle and pistol mixed team events. Rosters for 2028 are not set, and mixed pairs depend on which shooters each nation picks.

potentialContenders.name: Sheng Lihao
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 air rifle mixed team world title with Wang Zifei. Likely contender if he makes the team.

potentialContenders.name: Ban Hyojin
potentialContenders.note: Qualified first in Doha with Park Hajun, then took bronze. Could return for Korea if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Haniyeh Rostamiyan

SHO05.blurb:
This is medal day for skeet. Qualification wraps up in the morning, then the finals decide gold in both men's and women's skeet, each now with a field of eight rather than Paris 2024's six.

The biggest storyline is Vincent Hancock's bid for a fifth gold, which would be a first in Games history. He has said he expected to retire after Paris but could not pass up a home Games, and he must still earn his U.S. place.

Denmark's Jesper Hansen is the reigning men's world champion, and China's Jiang Yiting leads the women after her 2026 world title. Samantha Simonton and Francisca Crovetto add more name recognition if they qualify.

At Whittier Narrows, spectators sit in temporary stands behind the stations, with seating planned for about 2,000. New viewing technology is meant to help fans follow each target. A home-crowd roar for a U.S. shooter could carry across the range.
SHO05.potentialContendersIntro: These contenders cover the men's and women's skeet finals. Paris 2024 and 2026 world results are confirmed, but who actually reaches the 2028 final is speculation.

potentialContenders.name: Vincent Hancock
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist who hit all 36 targets in the final at the 2026 Lonato World Cup. A fifth gold would be a first in Games history. He is not yet confirmed for 2028.

potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champion, who beat Egypt's Azmy Mehelba 16-15 in a shoot-off after both hit 34. A projected men's medal contender if he competes.

potentialContenders.name: Samantha Simonton

potentialContenders.name: Francisca Crovetto
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 women's champion. If she qualifies, she could try to defend her title in the new eight-shooter final.

SHO06.blurb:
The men's 50m rifle three positions is the marathon of rifle shooting. This year's final has a new format: kneeling and prone are merged into one time-limited phase, with standing and elimination deciding the medals.

China's Liu Yukun, the Paris 2024 champion, also won the 2025 world title in Cairo by just 0.2 over India's Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar. Teammate Zhang Changhong set a final world record of 363.0 at a 2026 World Cup.

Qualification and the final both happen in one morning and early-afternoon session in Long Beach. The venue lets spectators follow each shot in a calm indoor setting.

SHO07.blurb:
Women's 50m rifle three positions is the longest test of nerve in the rifle events. A Doha 2026 final was settled on the last shot, and Serbia's Aleksandra Stojadinovic took gold by 0.7.

For 2028 the final is standing-only after kneeling and prone become one timed phase. That puts extra weight on the standing position, where steadiness can swing medals.

Paris 2024 champion Chiara Leone of Switzerland was fifth in Doha. In Long Beach, the session runs from morning to early afternoon and the hall stays hushed as the medal shots come down to the wire.
SHO07.potentialContendersIntro: Doha 2026 put Serbia, Korea and Japan on the quota board for this event. Paris 2024 medalists Chiara Leone and Sagen Maddalena could be back if they qualify, though 2028 rosters are not set.

SHO08.blurb:
Trap shooting begins here, with women and men shooting the first day of qualification. This is an accessible way to see the sport at work before the medal day.

The 2028 trap final takes eight athletes, not six. Day 1 is where shooters need a clean, steady score to stay in the hunt for a top-eight spot.

Whittier Narrows is a public clay range in the San Gabriel Valley, and the 2028 setup adds expanded temporary seating. Trap targets fly away from the shooter, so you can follow each flight from the stands.
SHO08.potentialContendersIntro: Trap has been open lately. Croatia's Josip Glasnovic and Spain's Mar Molne Magrina are the reigning 2025 world champions, and the 2028 fields are still projections.

potentialContenders.name: Mar Molne Magrina

potentialContenders.name: Silvana Stanco

potentialContenders.name: Nathan Hales

SHO09.blurb:
This is the first of two days for the 25m pistol events, and it is an accessible way into the sport. The men's rapid fire pistol stage 1 and the women's 25m pistol precision stage take place side by side.

Qualification is where the field is cut. For 2028 the rapid fire final grows from six to eight shooters. France's Clement Bessaguet set a qualification world record of 594 in May 2026.

The session runs from morning to late afternoon. In the Long Beach hall, you can watch the lanes with the tempo and drama building toward Sunday's finals.
SHO09.potentialContendersIntro: This is a qualification session, so no medals are awarded. Contenders below are projected from 2026 results, and 2028 participation is not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Florian Peter

potentialContenders.name: Manu Bhaker

SHO10.blurb:
Trap medal day. Qualification wraps up in the morning, then eight women and eight men go to the line in their separate finals for gold, silver and bronze.

The finals are stacked with recent history. Great Britain's Nathan Hales won Paris 2024 with a Games-record final, missing only two of 50, and Guatemala's Adriana Ruano won her country's first gold. Neither is guaranteed a 2028 place.

The Whittier Narrows stands sit behind the shooters, so you hear the call, the shot and the crowd's reaction in quick succession. A single miss can change the final order.
SHO10.potentialContendersIntro: These names mix Paris 2024 medalists and 2025 results with projections. Trap quota places open at the November 2026 World Championship in Doha, so the 2028 field is not yet set.

potentialContenders.name: Will Hinton

potentialContenders.name: Nathan Hales

potentialContenders.name: Adriana Ruano

potentialContenders.name: Silvana Stanco
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist, 2025 world silver medalist and World Cup Final winner. Mar Molne Magrina of Spain, the 2025 world champion, is another name to watch.

SHO11.blurb:
Sunday brings two pistol medal events to one long day. The men's rapid fire pistol finishes stage 2 and moves into an eight-shooter final, while the women's 25m pistol completes its rapid fire stage and goes to its own final.

Florian Peter of Germany won the 2026 rapid fire world title with 33 hits, one ahead of France's Clement Bessaguet. Yang Jiin of South Korea set a final world record of 44 hits to win the women's title.

The hall in Long Beach should have the most dramatic atmosphere of the shooting week. Fast rapid-fire strings and tight finals are on offer, and two sets of medals are decided before night.

SHO12.blurb:
Mixed team trap is new to the 2028 Games, replacing the one-time mixed skeet event from Paris 2024. Teams of one woman and one man shoot qualification, and the top four advance to the final.

The final is also new. Instead of separate gold and bronze matches, all four teams shoot together, which ISSF says keeps every medal contender in the contest to the end.

That should make for a clear storyline from the stands at Whittier Narrows. Skeet shooters have called the switch disappointing, so this event is a fresh test for many trap specialists.
SHO12.potentialContendersIntro: Italy won the 2025 world mixed trap title, and the USA took bronze. No quota places for mixed trap are awarded at the 2026 Worlds, so the 2028 pairings are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Massimo Fabbrizi

potentialContenders.name: Alessandra Perilli

SKB01.blurb:
Twenty-two women's street skaters open the 2028 Games skateboarding program in the Sepulveda Basin, with an evening session that cuts the field down to finalists. It's a good way to see the full depth of the sport.

The Paris 2024 podium was Coco Yoshizawa (gold), Liz Akama (silver) and Rayssa Leal (bronze). Japan has since won both 2026 world titles, so the favorites are hard to pin down.

The course is open-air, in a park near the 405 and 101 freeways. Expect a relaxed prelim crowd, close-up views of the rails and ledges, and the first real nerves of the Games.

potentialContenders.name: Chloe Covell
potentialContenders.note: Won the Rome World Cup in both 2025 and 2026. A projected threat if she qualifies.

SKB02.blurb:
Wednesday morning belongs to the men's street field, as 22 skaters work through the preliminary round at Valley Complex 1. It's a daytime session with the whole sport on display.

Prelims here set up that night's final. The depth is deep: Paris 2024 gold went to Yuto Horigome, with Americans Jagger Eaton and Nyjah Huston taking silver and bronze.

A wave of young Japanese skaters has since taken over the world titles. If the U.S. skaters qualify, expect a loud home crowd in the Sepulveda Basin sun.

potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 World Skate Games title in Asuncion with his final attempt and the 2025 SLS Super Crown at 15. Likely contender if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.note: Won the March 2026 world title in Sao Paulo with 174.10. Could be a top qualifier.

potentialContenders.name: Yuto Horigome
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist and two-time champion. Recent worlds results were weaker, so his 2028 qualification is not assured.

potentialContenders.name: Nyjah Huston
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist. He fractured his skull in January 2026 and says he's aiming for 2028, but his return is not confirmed.

SKB03.blurb:
The women's street final is the evening headliner, with medals decided under the lights in the Sepulveda Basin. The best skaters from the prelims go head to head.

Finals in this format often come down to the last trick. Ibuki Matsumoto won Kitakyushu 2025 by just 0.22 points over Yumeka Oda.

Japan's depth is the main storyline. Yoshizawa and Akama went 1-2 in Paris 2024, and Oda and Matsumoto split the 2026 world titles, with Brazil's Rayssa Leal and Australia's Chloe Covell likely to push them.

The 8:30 pm start puts the course under the lights. Expect a late-night atmosphere and a crowd that reacts to every landed trick.
SKB03.potentialContendersIntro: The final field depends on 2028 qualification and the prelims. These are projected contenders based on 2026 form.

potentialContenders.name: Yumeka Oda

potentialContenders.name: Chloe Covell

SKB04.blurb:
Eight skaters, one evening, and a medal on the line in the Sepulveda Basin. The Men's Street Final at Valley Complex 1 brings skateboarding back to Southern California, where the sport grew up.

The format follows Paris: each skater's best run counts alongside their two highest single-trick scores. Paris showed how fast things can flip, as Yuto Horigome rose from fourth to gold with a nollie 270 bluntslide on his last trick.

The 2028 field is still unsettled. Japan has looked deep in 2026, but qualification runs through the World Skateboarding Rankings and a final Q-Series, so no 2028 spots are locked in yet.

Expect an open-air, temporary course near the 405 and 101 junction, with an 8:30 PM start that should put the final under evening light. It is the first time the San Fernando Valley has hosted Games events.
SKB04.potentialContendersIntro: Horigome won Paris 2024 gold, with Jagger Eaton (USA) silver and Nyjah Huston (USA) bronze. The names below are projections based on 2026 results, and none are confirmed for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Yuto Horigome
potentialContenders.note: Confirmed Paris 2024 gold medalist and Tokyo 2020 champion, and based in California. He was second at Tampa Pro in 2026. If he qualifies, he could chase a third straight title.

potentialContenders.name: Sora Shirai
potentialContenders.note: Won WST Rome in June 2026 with 177.92, the first qualifying event for 2028, and was ranked world No. 1 going in. A likely contender if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Sasaki Toa
potentialContenders.note: Two-time defending world champion, with the 2025 title won in Sao Paulo in March 2026. He has said he definitely wants to compete in 2028. Rome 2026 bronze medalist.

potentialContenders.name: Ginwoo Onodera
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 World Championships in Asuncion, his first WST event win. A rising name to watch if he makes the team.

potentialContenders.name: Nyjah Huston
potentialContenders.note: Confirmed Paris 2024 bronze medalist. Could appear if he qualifies and is a possible home-crowd favorite, though 2028 participation is not confirmed.

SKB05.blurb:
Twenty-two skaters drop into the bowl at Valley Complex 2 for the men's park preliminary, and only the top group moves on to the final. It is the first chance to see the sport's biggest names under pressure.

The field is projected to be deep. Reigning champion Keegan Palmer (AUS) will try to extend his title streak if he qualifies, while Spain's Egoitz Bijueska, the 2026 world champion, is a likely threat.

The venue is a temporary open-air park inside the Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area. A morning prelim is a relaxed way to catch a skate session and explore the other Valley Zone venues in the same trip.
SKB05.potentialContendersIntro: Palmer won gold at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024. Qualification is not settled until the June 2028 ranking, so this list is projected from recent form.

potentialContenders.name: Keegan Palmer
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist with a 93.11 first run. If he qualifies, he is chasing a third straight title, though his 2026 form was mixed.

potentialContenders.name: Egoitz Bijueska
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 world title in Asuncion with 94.50 and the 2025 title in Sao Paulo. He turns 16 in November 2026 and is a projected contender if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Tom Schaar
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist and silver at the 2026 Asuncion worlds with 93.07. Could draw strong home-crowd support.

potentialContenders.name: Gui Khury

potentialContenders.name: Augusto Akio
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and fourth in Asuncion in 2026 with 91.35. Could appear if he qualifies.

SKB06.blurb:
The women's park preliminary is a chance to see some of the highest-scoring skaters in the world in one evening session. With 22 skaters in the field, the cut to the final is tight.

The form guide is stacked. Japan's Mizuho Hasegawa posted a 96.33 run at the 2026 Rome World Cup, which World Skate called the highest women's park score on the World Skateboarding Tour.

Expect an evening crowd and a lively atmosphere around the bowl at Valley Complex 2. It is a good way to get a first look at the field before the final.
SKB06.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 produced a podium separated by under a point. Rosters for 2028 are not set, so these names are projected from recent form and are not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Mizuho Hasegawa
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 world title in Asuncion and the Rome World Cup with a 96.33 run. A leading projected contender if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Sky Brown
potentialContenders.note: Bronze at Paris 2024 and 2025 world champion. She was second at both Rome and Asuncion in 2026, and is working toward a third Games.

potentialContenders.name: Cocona Hiraki
potentialContenders.note: Silver medalist at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, third at the 2026 Rome World Cup. Japan is limited to three women, so a spot is not guaranteed.

potentialContenders.name: Arisa Trew
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist at age 14 and X Games Sacramento 2026 winner. Could be a favorite in her title defense if she qualifies.

SKB07.blurb:
The men's park final is a medal session where one clean run can decide everything. At Paris 2024, only two of eight finalists landed their opening runs, and Keegan Palmer's first-run 93.11 held up.

Palmer has won both men's park golds so far, and a third would make it three in a row. Challengers include Spain's Egoitz Bijueska, the 2026 world champion, along with Tom Schaar and Gui Khury, if they qualify.

The final is an evening session at Valley Complex 2 in the Sepulveda Basin. Expect a loud crowd, a long run of high-risk tricks, and a quick 75 minutes.
SKB07.potentialContendersIntro: The final lineup depends on the June 2028 World Skateboarding Ranking, so these contenders are projected from recent results and not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Keegan Palmer
potentialContenders.note: Gold at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024. His 2026 form was mixed (X Games silver, bronze, fourth), but he is a proven big-event skater if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.note: Back-to-back world champion with 95.83 in Sao Paulo and 94.50 in Asuncion. Has called competing at the Games a childhood dream; projected contender if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Tom Schaar
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist and silver at the 2026 Asuncion worlds with 93.07. Could be the top American in the final.

potentialContenders.name: Gui Khury

potentialContenders.name: Gavin Bottger
potentialContenders.note: 2023 world champion from Oceanside, California, and X Games gold medalist in 2025 and 2026. A possible home-state favorite if he qualifies.

SKB08.blurb:
The women's park final is expected to be one of the most competitive finals on the skateboarding schedule. At Paris 2024, just 0.87 points separated gold from bronze.

Arisa Trew won at Paris at age 14 with 93.18. Since then, Mizuho Hasegawa has posted a 96.33 run and won the 2026 world title, while Sky Brown and Cocona Hiraki remain in the medal picture.

The session runs on a Thursday evening at Valley Complex 2 in the Sepulveda Basin. Expect a loud, close-up atmosphere around the bowl as the medals are decided.
SKB08.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gold went to Trew, silver to Hiraki and bronze to Brown. The 2028 field depends on the June 2028 ranking, so these names are projected and not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Arisa Trew

potentialContenders.name: Mizuho Hasegawa
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champion in Asuncion and Rome World Cup winner with a 96.33 run. Projected favorite if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Sky Brown
potentialContenders.note: Bronze at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, world champion in 2023 and 2025, and second at both Rome and Asuncion in 2026. A likely medal threat if she competes.

potentialContenders.name: Cocona Hiraki

SQU01.blurb:
Squash's first night on a Summer Games program opens with the Round of 16 under the lights at Universal Studios. Every match is single elimination, so a loss on opening night ends a player's tournament.

Four matches span the men's and women's draws. Malaysia's Ng Eain Yow and Sivasangari Subramaniam are already qualified as 2026 Asian Games champions, and Egyptian stars such as Mostafa Asal and Amina Orfi lead the world rankings.

The temporary courts sit on the studio backlot, with film-set facades behind the stands. Expect a late-evening, 7:30 pm start and a crowd taking in a brand-new Games sport.
SQU01.potentialContendersIntro: The draws are not set, and which night a player appears depends on the bracket. Qualified names and world rankings give a sense of who could take the court.

potentialContenders.name: Ng Eain Yow
potentialContenders.note: Confirmed qualifier after winning the 2026 Asian Games men's gold; ranked 17th in October 2026. Draw slot to be determined.

potentialContenders.name: Sivasangari Subramaniam
potentialContenders.note: Confirmed qualifier as 2026 Asian Games women's champion, beating India's Anahat Singh in the final.

potentialContenders.name: Mostafa Asal
potentialContenders.note: World No. 1 in October 2026 rankings and reigning world champion; projected to qualify, not yet confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Amina Orfi
potentialContenders.note: Became the youngest women's world No. 1 at 19 in September 2026; a projected top seed if she qualifies.

SQU02.blurb:
Night two of the Round of 16 brings another four knockout matches, and again every loser goes home after a single match. Early rounds can be lopsided, since universality places are part of the draws.

The two-players-per-country cap shapes the field. Egypt holds four of the top seven men in the rankings but can send only two, so some elite names will watch from home.

Spectators sit in temporary stands on the studio backlot, a setting unlike any traditional squash venue. The evening session runs roughly 7:30 to 11:15 pm.
SQU02.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected names only; qualification is still open. Players below could appear on any Round of 16 night, depending on the draw.

potentialContenders.name: Anahat Singh
potentialContenders.note: At 18 and ranked 15th, she beat eight-time world champion Nour El Sherbini 3-0 in October 2026. A dangerous floater if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Nour El Sherbini

potentialContenders.name: Olivia Weaver
potentialContenders.note: World No. 4 in June 2026 and a 2024 and 2025 world semifinalist. A possible home contender, but her June 2026 injury is a question mark.

potentialContenders.name: Mohamad Zakaria

SQU03.blurb:
By the third night the Round of 16 is in full swing, and the bracket is steadily thinning toward the quarterfinals. Every result here is a first for squash at the Games.

The field is still unsettled. One place per gender is decided at a June 2028 qualifier in Seattle, while the other 15 players in each draw come through Continental Games, rankings and universality places.

Courthouse Square, the backlot set seen in Back to the Future, serves as the backdrop. It is an unusual mix of squash intensity and Hollywood scenery.
SQU03.potentialContendersIntro: Qualification is unfinished, so these are projections based on October 2026 rankings, except where noted as already qualified.

potentialContenders.note: Already qualified as two-time Asian Games champion; ranked 17th in October 2026.

SQU04.blurb:
The Round of 16 wraps up tonight, completing the eight quarterfinal places in both draws. Anyone still standing after this session is just two wins from a medal match.

The field reflects a system built to balance top-ranked players with wide national representation. Four-time world champion Ali Farag retired in 2025 and will not be in the draw, which leaves the men's field more open.

A late-evening finish on the backlot gives the night real tournament tension. Fans get a final look at the early rounds before the stakes rise.
SQU04.potentialContendersIntro: Nothing is settled for 2028. These are projected contenders based on recent results.

potentialContenders.note: 2024 world champion and world No. 3 in October 2026; projected to compete if he qualifies.

SQU05.blurb:
The quarterfinals begin, and the first four matches send winners into the medal round. Losers leave without a medal, while semifinal losers still get a bronze match.

This is where the Egyptian depth in the rankings and the two-per-country cap create the biggest storylines. Mostafa Asal is a two-time reigning men's world champion, and the women's world titles have been shared by Egyptians recently.

The backlot stands should be loud for these matches, with quarterfinal tension filling the late-evening air.
SQU05.potentialContendersIntro: Contenders below are projections for the men's and women's draws. Egypt can enter only two per gender, so not every Egyptian listed can make it.

SQU06.blurb:
The second quarterfinal night fills out both semifinal lineups. By the end, the four men and four women still alive are guaranteed at least a shot at a bronze medal.

The session can open a door for non-Egyptian players. Paul Coll, Diego Elias and Sivasangari Subramaniam are among those who could push into the semifinals.

With every medal in the tournament a first for squash, the quarterfinals carry historic weight. The backlot setting adds a cinematic feel as the draw narrows.
SQU06.potentialContendersIntro: Projected names only, since the draw is not set. These players could appear in the quarterfinals if they qualify, except where noted.

The women's semifinals carry a guaranteed medal match for each loser, so the winners go for gold and the losers for bronze. It is the first time medals will be decided in squash at a Summer Games.

Egyptian women have won recent world titles: Nouran Gohar in 2024, Nour El Sherbini in 2025 and Amina Orfi in 2026. The two-per-country cap means at most two Egyptians can be in the draw.

Expect a hushed, intense crowd between rallies at the backlot courts, with an 8:30 pm start and a late finish.

The men's semifinals decide who plays for gold and who drops to the bronze match. Both Asal and Coll have been dominant in the lead-up, and the draw could produce a clash of styles.

Egypt holds four of the top seven men in the rankings but can enter only two. That makes a non-Egyptian semifinalist very likely, with Coll and Elias leading the outside threats.

The backlot courts give a sold-out evening a sense of occasion, with only two matches and the bigger finish near 11:15 pm.

SQU09.blurb:
The first women's squash medals in Games history are decided tonight, with the bronze medal match followed by the gold. It is a historic moment for a sport that waited a long time for this stage.

Egypt has won every recent women's world title, but the two-player cap prevents a podium sweep unless both qualifiers reach the medal matches. That leaves room for Malaysia's Sivasangari Subramaniam or the United States' Olivia Weaver to disrupt the favorites.

The medal matches take place on the Courthouse Square backlot, a setting few venues could match. Expect a charged, late-night atmosphere through to 11:30 pm.

SQU10.blurb:
The final session closes out squash's first Games tournament with the men's bronze medal match, then the gold. It is the last squash action of the 2028 Games.

Asal, a two-time world champion, is the projected favorite if he qualifies, but Coll and Elias have beaten the top Egyptians in major finals. With at most two Egyptian men allowed, the podium will include at least one other nationality.

The closing night should feel like a celebration on the Universal backlot, with Courthouse Square as a backdrop and the first men's squash medals on the line.

SRF01.blurb:
The first morning of surfing at Lower Trestles opens with Round 1 for both men and women. It is the full 48-surfer field's first look at the cobblestone point, so expect a lot of unfamiliar names.

The field will not be fully known until shortly before the Games. Universality places could bring surfers from smaller surfing nations alongside the sport's established stars.

There are no permanent grandstands at this state beach. Fans watch from sand and cobblestone close to the lineup, in a temporary setup with capacity capped well below a regular pro event.

SRF02.blurb:
Round 2 is where the bracket starts to bite. Surfers who stumbled in Round 1 now face a second chance, and the margin for error shrinks.

Lower Trestles has been a recent showcase for the Championship Tour. Miguel Pupo and Erin Brooks won there in 2026, and Brooks is a teenager on a three-event win streak.

Qualification is still unfolding, so the Round 2 field is not set. Expect a mix of tour regulars and qualifiers watching the cobblestone A-frames from a temporary beachside setup.

SRF03.blurb:
Round 3 narrows the field toward the quarterfinals, and the stakes rise with each heat. Anyone who falls short here is likely out of the medal race.

Countries can send up to three surfers per gender, so Brazil, Australia and the USA could have several surfers still alive. National rivalries may start to show up in the heat draws.

The 2026 Championship Tour gives a preview of likely storylines. Yago Dora and Molly Picklum led the rankings in late October 2026, and Carissa Moore sat second after returning to the tour.

Paris 2024 produced a 0.17-point women's final, with Caroline Marks edging Tatiana Weston-Webb. Kauli Vaast took men's gold over Jack Robinson, and Gabriel Medina and Johanne Defay won bronze.

Trestles gives surfers home advantage, as several San Clemente locals grew up on this wave. Fans on the sand will be watching close to the lineup, and the exact running order will depend on conditions.

SWA01.blurb:
The 2028 artistic swimming program opens in Long Beach with the women's duet technical routine. This morning prelim puts the first set of scores on the board.

Duets perform a routine built around required elements, and the score carries into Wednesday's free routine. Austria's Alexandri twins won the 2025 world technical title, and China's new pairing of Lin Yanjun and Xu Huiyan won the 2026 World Cup Super Final.

The temporary open-air pool sits on the Long Beach Convention Center grounds near the downtown waterfront. Expect coastal summer weather and a crowd getting its first look at the sport at these Games.

SWA02.blurb:
This is the duet medal session. The free routine, performed with fewer restrictions on choreography and music, is added to Tuesday's technical score to decide the podium.

China's Wang twins won Paris 2024 gold, and Great Britain's Shortman and Thorpe took silver. Spain's Iris Tio Casas and Lilou Lluis Valette won the 2025 world free title. China's Lin Yanjun and Xu Huiyan won the 2026 World Cup Super Final free.

The open-air Long Beach pool puts spectators close to the water, so the music, the synchronized rhythm and the splash of each routine carry through the venue. It is a good late-morning medal session.

SWA03.blurb:
The team event begins with the technical routine. Eight swimmers, up to two of them men, perform required elements in unison, and this is the first of three scores that add up to the team medal.

China won the 2025 world team technical title and the 2026 World Cup Super Final technical. Spain and the neutral-athlete squads have been the nearest challengers, and the United States is building toward 2028.

The session is short at 90 minutes and easy to attend. The pool sits in a temporary open-air stadium, and the large teams make the formations and lifts easier to see.

SWA04.blurb:
The team free routine is the second of three team scores. Creative choreography, theme and musicality matter more here than in the technical routine, and the rankings can shift.

China has won the world team free title every year from 2022 through 2025, and led Paris 2024 after this stage. Japan and Spain were the 2025 runners-up, and the United States hopes to move up from just off the podium.

The sport returns to the Los Angeles area, where it debuted at the 1984 Games. Expect an open-air Long Beach crowd and a themed routine that fills most of the pool.

SWA05.blurb:
The team acrobatic routine closes artistic swimming at the 2028 Games and decides the team medals. Scores from the technical, free and acrobatic routines are combined for the final standings.

Acrobatics means throws, lifts and high-risk flips, so a single miss can reshape the podium. China sealed its first team gold in this routine in Paris 2024, and whether it can defend that title is a central storyline.

The session runs from 10:45 AM to 12:30 PM at the Long Beach pool. The crowd should be loud as the lifts and the final medal scores come in.

SWM01.blurb:
The pool opens at 2028 Stadium with a morning heat session, and the first heats of the new men's 50m butterfly and women's 50m backstroke. Those two events were approved in April 2025 and use heats, semifinals and a final.

Also on deck are heats of the women's 100m fly, men's 400m free, men's 100m breast and women's 400m free. The men's and women's 4x100m free relay heats go straight to that evening's finals, so they set the lanes.

A 50-meter pool on an NFL stadium floor under a translucent canopy is a striking setting. Morning heats are an easy, lower-key way to see the deck and the giant ring-shaped video board.

SWM02.blurb:
The first finals night of swimming arrives with four medal races: the men's and women's 400m freestyle and both 4x100m freestyle relays. Semifinals fill out the rest, including the new men's 50m fly and women's 50m back.

The women's 400m free will crown a new champion, since Ariarne Titmus retired in October 2025. Summer McIntosh, the Paris 2024 silver medalist, beat Katie Ledecky at the 2025 Worlds, so this could be a close fight.

The relays carry real rivalry. The US men won in Paris and the Australian women won the women's race, and Australia beat the US by 0.66 seconds in the 2025 women's 4x200m relay.

Expect a loud crowd under the canopy on opening night, with the whole pool visible from the stands.

Day two opens with a morning heat session at the 2028 Stadium. It covers the women's 100m breaststroke, men's 100m backstroke, women's 100m freestyle and the men's 400m IM.

The 400m IM skips semifinals, so only the top eight this morning make that evening's final. Léon Marchand, the Paris 2024 champion, is the name to watch if he swims it.

The pool sits on the stadium floor, with the huge ring-shaped video board overhead. Morning heats are easy to get into, and you can see future medalists before the evening crowds arrive.

SWM04.blurb:
Six medal events in two hours make this a dense night in the pool. Gold goes out in the women's 100m butterfly, men's 400m IM, men's 100m breaststroke and the new men's 50m butterfly and women's 50m backstroke.

The two new 50m finals will be the first medal races in those events at the Games. Gretchen Walsh, who won the 2025 world title in 54.73, could renew her 100m butterfly duel with Paris 2024 champion Torri Huske.

Semifinals in the women's 100m breaststroke, men's 100m backstroke and women's 100m freestyle add to the evening. It is a fast-moving program under the lights, with the pool far below the stadium seating.

Day three's heats are loaded with big names. The women's 400m IM and men's 1500m free go straight to finals, and the men's 200m free, 200m fly, women's 100m back and new men's 50m breaststroke feed semifinals.

Summer McIntosh won the 400m IM at Paris 2024 and again at the 2025 Worlds, where she took four golds. David Popovici, the Paris 2024 and 2025 world 200m free champion, is the man to chase.

The men's 1500m heats test endurance, with Ahmed Jaouadi's 800m world title in 2025 hinting at a distance shake-up.

Session seating is easy in the morning, and it makes a good chance to see future finalists up close.

Monday's finals session is a sprint-heavy night, with medals in the women's 100m freestyle, men's 100m backstroke, women's 100m breaststroke and women's 400m IM.

The 400m IM is where Summer McIntosh could shine, as Paris 2024 gold medalist and 2025 world champion. The 100m freestyle brings Sarah Sjöström's Paris 2024 gold into a field that could include Gretchen Walsh and Kate Douglass.

Men's 200m freestyle, women's 100m backstroke, men's 50m breaststroke and men's 200m butterfly semifinals fill out the night. Expect a loud crowd and a pool glowing against the stadium's open sides.

Tuesday's morning session is a low-pressure chance to see big names in heats. It features the women's 200m freestyle, men's 50m freestyle, women's 200m breaststroke and women's 1500m freestyle.

The 1500m freestyle goes straight to the final, so these heats set the lineup. Katie Ledecky, the Paris 2024 champion and 2025 world champion in 15:26.44, would be the swimmer to watch.

The 50m freestyle is over in about 21 seconds, so the heats are quick. Seats near the walls show the starts and turns, and you can watch the swimmers warm up in a big pool.

Tuesday night has a stacked slate: finals in the men's 200m freestyle, 1500m freestyle, 200m butterfly and women's 100m backstroke. The new men's 50m breaststroke also awards its first medal at the Games.

If Adam Peaty swims it, he holds the 25.95 world record from 2017, but he missed the 2026 European semifinals in 27.34. The men's 200m freestyle may feature Paris 2024 gold medalist David Popovici.

Three semifinals round out the night. The 1500m is a long, quiet-then-roaring race that rewards patience in the stands.

Day five's morning has men's 200m IM, men's 200m back and the new women's 50m butterfly heats. The men's 4x200m free relay goes straight to that evening's final.

Léon Marchand won the 200m IM at Paris 2024, and Hubert Kós won 200m back gold. Great Britain won Paris 2024 relay gold ahead of the US and Australia.

The relay heats will show who gets the eight lanes. Popovici, Hobson and Japan's Tatsuya Murasa suggest several nations could be contenders.

Arrive early for the new women's 50m fly heats and a first look at the sport's newest events.

Wednesday night ends with a relay, the men's 4x200m freestyle final, where Great Britain won at Paris 2024. Earlier events include the women's 200m freestyle, men's 50m freestyle, women's 200m breaststroke and women's 1500m freestyle finals.

The 200m breaststroke could be a showcase: Kate Douglass, Paris 2024 champion, and Tatjana Smith, back for the Netherlands, could renew their rivalry. Ledecky's 1500m could add a late highlight.

Semifinals in the men's 200m IM, men's 200m backstroke and the new women's 50m butterfly add depth. With five finals in two hours, the stadium has constant noise.

Pan Zhanle won Paris 2024 gold in the 100m free in a world record, and Kaylee McKeown won the 200m back and won it again at the 2025 Worlds.

Australia won the women's 4x200m relay at Paris 2024 and the 2025 Worlds, with the US second both times by a narrow margin. The world record belongs to Australia at 7:37.50.

Heats can be a good way to spot who might surprise on the later nights.

Day six's finals include the men's 200m back, women's 50m fly, men's 200m IM and women's 4x200m free relay. The women's 50m fly is a new event, so it awards its first Games medal.

Gretchen Walsh won the 2025 world 50m fly title in 24.83, and she won the 100m too. Léon Marchand set a 200m IM world record of 1:52.69 in 2025.

Hubert Kós won 200m back at Paris 2024 and 2025 Worlds. Australia won the relay in both and beat the US by under a second in 2025.

The event sequence is quick, with four medal races and several semifinals.

The mixed medley relay was won by the US in Paris 2024, ahead of China and Australia.

Morning heats give a relaxed look at new events while the men's 800m field sorts itself out.

A morning crowd can be thinner, but the stadium still feels huge. It is a chance to see world-record-caliber swimmers up close.

Women's -57kg has a clear storyline: Brazil's Maria Clara Pacheco beat Paris 2024 champion Kim Yu-jin for the 2025 world title. Whether that rivalry continues in Los Angeles remains to be seen.

TKW06.blurb:
This evening decides the men's -68kg and women's -57kg medals through repechages, two bronze medal contests per category and two gold medal contests. It is the second finals night of taekwondo at the 2028 Games.

In the men's division, Uzbekistan's Ulugbek Rashitov won gold at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024. A third title would require him to return and qualify after his suspension ends in May 2027.

In women's -57kg, Paris 2024 champion Kim Yu-jin of South Korea faces a challenge from Brazil's Maria Clara Pacheco, who won the 2025 world title. Night sessions in Hall 1 have the biggest crowd, with fans close to the mats.

The third day of competition opens with women's -67kg and men's -80kg in the Round of 32 and Round of 16. The weight classes are heavier and rounds can be more explosive.

Hungary has strong momentum in women's -67kg. Viviana Marton won Paris 2024 gold, and Luana Marton, age 19, won the 2025 world title.

Men's -80kg is more open. Brazil's Henrique Marques won the 2025 world title, and Belarus' Raman Turavinau won the Muju 2026 Grand Prix. The morning is a good chance to scout rising fighters.

TKW08.blurb:
Women's -67kg and men's -80kg reach the semifinal stage, with bronze contests and the finals only hours away. Semifinal winners advance to gold, and the rest drop into the repechage.

In women's -67kg, Hungary's Marton name looms large, and Brazil's Milena Titoneli reached the 2025 world final. Men's -80kg features names that have already been in finals: Paris 2024 champion Firas Katoussi and 2025 world champion Henrique Marques.

As a semifinal session in Hall 1, expect a lively atmosphere, with strong fan sections from many countries. Matches can be tight, with comebacks that change the bracket.

TKW09.blurb:
The first week of taekwondo ends tonight with women's -67kg and men's -80kg. Repechages, bronze contests and gold medal contests fill the evening.

Hungary could be a headline team: Viviana Marton won Paris 2024 gold, and Luana Marton won the 2025 world title. But one country normally gets one fighter per category, so they may be competing for the same spot.

Men's -80kg could feature Paris 2024 champion Firas Katoussi and 2025 world champion Henrique Marques. Hall 1 should feel like a final-night crowd, with chants and flags close to the mats.

The final day of taekwondo starts with men's +80kg Round of 32 and Round of 16, plus the women's +67kg Round of 16. The heavyweights bring big kicks and plenty of momentum swings.

Iran's Arian Salimi is the Paris 2024 men's +80kg champion. The women's heavyweight picture is unsettled: France's Althea Laurin, the Paris champion, was reported suspended for 20 months over missed tests, with no return date given.

That makes the women's draw hard to predict. This is a morning session in Hall 1 with the weight classes mixed together.

Quarterfinals and semifinals for men's +80kg and women's +67kg. Semifinal losers drop into bronze medal contests later the same day, and fighters beaten by the finalists enter repechage.

In Paris, the heavyweight medal rounds were also held on the final Saturday at the Grand Palais, where Laurin won the women's gold and Salimi the men's. Whether those champions will compete in 2028 is not confirmed.

The heavyweights are the sport's biggest fighters, and the Hall 1 crowd is likely to be at its peak by the afternoon. It is a good session for fans who want knockout stakes before the finals.

The last night of taekwondo decides the men's +80kg and women's +67kg medals, through repechages, two bronze contests per category and both gold medal fights. It closes the sport's 2028 program.

In Paris, Salimi beat Cunningham for men's gold, and Laurin beat Osipova 2-0 with a high kick in the final seconds. Neither champion has been confirmed for 2028, so these results are history rather than a forecast.

Expect a big-night feel in the convention hall: the fighting area is lit up inside the 7,000-seat bowl. Combining both categories makes this a full evening of medal action.

TRI01.blurb:
The women's individual triathlon is scheduled to award the first medals of the 2028 Games, a 7:30 AM start on the sand. It would be the first time triathlon has opened the medal schedule since Sydney 2000.

Athletes run into the Pacific for a 1,500m swim in two laps with a 25m beach run in between. Then come eight 5km bike laps with two technical turnarounds and a four-lap 10km run near the Venice canals.

The transition area and finish sit where Venice Boulevard meets the sand, with limited grandstand seating. Spectators can also line the course near the boardwalk and Muscle Beach, so expect a loose, beachfront crowd early on a Saturday morning.
TRI01.potentialContendersIntro: Cassandre Beaugrand (FRA) won Paris 2024 gold, and the names below are projections based on recent form. None are confirmed for 2028, since qualification runs through the May 2028 ranking.

potentialContenders.name: Cassandre Beaugrand
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champion who went unbeaten in the 2026 WTCS season and won the Pontevedra Grand Final. A likely favorite if she holds this form.

potentialContenders.name: Lisa Tertsch
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion, and runner-up to Beaugrand at WTCS London in 2026. Projected to be a podium threat.

potentialContenders.name: Léonie Périault
potentialContenders.note: Second in the final 2025 WTCS standings and a member of France's 2026 world-title relay team. Could give France a second medal threat.

potentialContenders.name: Beth Potter
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and third in the 2025 WTCS standings. Could return to the podium if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Taylor Knibb
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 Ironman World Championship in Kona and is collecting 2028 qualification points. A home-crowd storyline to watch if she makes the US team.

TRI02.blurb:
The men's individual race follows the women's the next morning, a 7:30 AM start on Venice Beach. It is a single final with no heats, so one race decides the medals.

The field charges into the surf for a two-lap 1.5km swim. Then comes an eight-lap 40km bike with two technical turnarounds and a four-lap 10km run through the Venice canals area.

The loop course lets fans on the boardwalk and around Muscle Beach see athletes pass many times. The finish at Venice Boulevard and the sand gives a close-up view of any sprint, and recent men's races have been decided by fractions of a second.
TRI02.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gold went to Alex Yee (GBR), ahead of Hayden Wilde (NZL) and Léo Bergère (FRA). The list below is projected from 2026 form, and 2028 participation is not confirmed.

potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion who beat Vilaça by 0.08 seconds at the 2026 Pontevedra Grand Final. A projected favorite in a sprint finish.

potentialContenders.name: Vasco Vilaça
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champion and a repeated runner-up to Hauser in close finishes. Likely a leading medal contender.

potentialContenders.name: Morgan Pearson

TRI03.blurb:
The mixed relay closes the triathlon program, and it is the sport's last medal event of the 2028 Games. Teams of two women and two men race in a quick, team-based format.

The order is women, men, women, men, the reverse of the men-first order used at Paris 2024. Each athlete does a 350m swim from the shoreline, a 6.6km bike over two 3.3km laps and a 1.6km run over two 800m laps.

The short laps keep the action close to the Venice Beach crowd, and exchanges happen in front of the grandstand. Paris 2024 came down to a three-way sprint, so a tight finish seems likely again.
TRI03.potentialContendersIntro: Germany won Paris 2024, ahead of the United States and Great Britain. Only the United States, as host, has a confirmed 2028 place so far. The other teams below are projected contenders, and rosters are not set.

potentialContenders.name: Germany

potentialContenders.name: Great Britain

TTE01.blurb:
The table tennis tournament opens with a double bill. The men's and women's singles round of 64 shares the morning with the mixed doubles round of 16, the first eliminations of the Games' six-event program.

Singles is single elimination from here, so one bad set can end a run. Mixed doubles pairs also play with no safety net, which suits fast, tactical partnerships.

Hall 3 is a converted exhibit hall at the Convention Center, so fans sit close to the tables. Expect the squeak of shoes and the crack of the ball, with early upsets always possible.

TTE02.blurb:
Men's and women's doubles are back on the Games program for the first time since 2004, and this session is where they start. Both draws open at the round of 16.

The format rewards chemistry as much as raw talent. Doubles matches were best of five at the 2025 World Championships, and partners alternate shots, so a well-drilled pair can upset a more famous one.

In Hall 3 you will be close to the action. Expect plenty of tight, fast exchanges across several tables.

Saturday night brings a men's and women's singles round of 64 session. It is an accessible way to catch the sport's depth and spot the players who could trouble the favorites.

The field is fresh and the bracket is wide open. Japan's Sora Matsushima reached world No. 1 in October 2026, the first Japanese man there since Seiji Ono in 1980.

Expect a tight, loud room in Hall 3 as the evening session builds. Seats are close to the action, and capacity is likely to be limited.

Sunday morning pairs the mixed doubles quarterfinals with more singles round-of-64 action. It is the first time a medal chase starts to feel real in Hall 3.

Mixed doubles at the 2025 World Championships was best of five games, and short formats like that reward pairs who find rhythm quickly. China won the Paris 2024 gold, with North Korea taking silver and South Korea bronze.

With tables set close to the seating, you can read the partnerships up close: the signals, the switches and the shared reactions after big points.

This afternoon session is a men's and women's singles round of 64, with plenty of tables in play. It is a good chance to see the early rounds, where one off day ends a run.

Paris 2024 showed how fast that can happen. Sweden's Truls Möregårdh knocked out the top seed on his way to the final, the tournament's biggest upset.

Hall 3 is intimate by Games standards, so even early-round matches feel close. Expect pockets of national flags and loud support from fans of the lower-profile players.

Sunday night brings the mixed doubles semifinals, with only a handful of pairs left. Singles round-of-64 matches fill out the session around them.

The event is led by China's two-pair depth. Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha won gold in Paris and then won the 2025 world title 3-1 over Japan's Yoshimura and Odo.

Semifinal nights in a hall this size are electric. Fans sit within a few steps of the table, and every long rally gets a reaction.

Doubles quarterfinals for both men and women make this a showcase for the returning events. With the singles round of 64 alongside, the hall stays busy all morning.

The field is open. China did not win men's doubles at the 2025 World Championships, and a deep field of Japanese, French and Chinese pairs could make these matches close.

Quarterfinals in Hall 3 offer a front-row-feeling look at doubles tactics. Watch the rotation between partners as they move around the table.

TTE08.blurb:
Monday's afternoon session is another men's and women's singles round of 64. It is a low-pressure way to sample the sport, with stars and unknowns on adjacent tables.

France's Félix Lebrun, the Paris 2024 bronze medalist, is among the names to watch. He was ranked No. 2 in October 2026 and won WTT Champions Chongqing that year.

The host country's players are always a draw, and the USA's top man, Kanak Jha, was ranked No. 24 in October 2026. If he qualifies, Hall 3 will likely get loud for him.

TTE09.blurb:
Monday night brings the first table tennis medals of the Games: the mixed doubles bronze and gold medal matches. It is a ready-made reason to book an evening.

China won this event in Paris, beating North Korea for gold, with South Korea taking bronze. Whether anyone can break China's hold on the sport is the main storyline for 2028.

Expect a full house in Hall 3, close to the table, with flags and chants. A bronze match followed by a gold match makes for a long and emotional night.

potentialContenders.name: Lim Jong-hoon / Shin Yu-bin

TTE10.blurb:
Men's doubles returns for the first time since 2004, and its semifinals headline Tuesday morning. Singles round-of-32 matches fill the other tables.

Doubles asks for a different skill than singles: serve-and-receive choreography and quick switches between partners. Teams with a shared history, like France's Lebrun brothers, bring an edge.

Watching doubles in Hall 3 is a close-up lesson in teamwork. Round-of-32 singles on adjacent tables add to the morning.

Tuesday afternoon is a men's and women's singles round of 32, where seeds start to meet tougher opponents. The bracket begins to tighten.

This is also the first Games without Chen Meng in women's singles, as she indicated Paris would be her last. The title is wide open.

Hall 3 sits inside the Los Angeles Convention Center, so the feel is more tournament hall than arena. Seats are limited, which makes tickets a premium.

There is no defending champion, and China did not win the 2025 world title. That makes this one of China's less certain chances at gold, and Japan and France are projected threats.

The final in Hall 3 should feel like a close, loud arena. A late finish makes for a strong cap to the day.

Sweden's Truls Möregårdh is a storyline. The Paris 2024 silver medalist won WTT Champions Macao in September 2026, though an injury forced his Frankfurt withdrawal.

Hall 3 gets louder as the stakes rise, with flags from every continent. Matches run in quick succession across the tables.

Japan's Sora Matsushima rose to world No. 1 in October 2026 and lost the Men's World Cup final 4-3 to Wang Chuqin. China also won both team titles at the 2026 World Team Championships, so the favorite's pressure is real.

The round of 16 in a hall this size has real intensity. Fans can follow every rally from close range.

The quarterfinal crowd in Hall 3 is close and loud. It is a prime session for fans who want serious stakes without a final-day ticket.

Eight players per draw become four in this afternoon quarterfinal session, which settles the last semifinal places in both men's and women's singles. Every match is single elimination, so one bad game can end a medal run.

Expect a mix of storylines. The men's side has been wide open lately, with Japan's Sora Matsushima reaching world No. 1 and France's Félix Lebrun ranked No. 2 as of October 2026.

Hall 3 is an exhibit hall turned arena, so seats sit close to the tables. You will hear every ball strike, and the crowd noise comes in loud bursts after long rallies.

The men's field looks wide open. Wang Chuqin holds the 2025 world title and the 2026 World Cup, but Hugo Calderano beat him at the 2025 World Cup, and Jang Woojin won WTT Champions Montpellier in 2026.

A wild card is Fan Zhendong, the Paris 2024 champion. He left the world rankings in December 2024 and has not said whether he will try for 2028.

The late slot in a small, close hall should feel loud and tight, with spectators almost within arm's reach of the tables.

Four women remain, and two will play for gold. The women's singles semifinals are a single-elimination test where one hot streak or one cold game can end a title chase.

Sun Yingsha is the benchmark. She won back-to-back world titles through 2025, swept three straight World Cups through 2026, and has held the No. 1 ranking for over 200 consecutive weeks. Even so, she has been pushed, including a seven-game World Cup scare from Japan's Hana Goda.

The two-per-country cap limits how many Chinese players can reach the last four. That opens room for Japan and others.

In Hall 3 the crowd sits close to the tables, so semifinal tension is easy to feel from nearly any seat.

Chen Meng, who beat Sun Yingsha in Paris, said that would be her last Games, so a new champion is expected. Sun, the Paris silver medalist, has been the most consistent contender since.

Challengers include Wang Manyu, who was runner-up to Sun at both the 2025 Worlds and the 2026 World Cup, and Kuai Man, who beat Sun once in 2026.

The closing session in a compact hall should feel like a final in a small-arena setting: close seats, long rallies and a loud finish.

Whether Fan returns is an open question. He left the world rankings in December 2024 and has not decided on 2028, though ITTF president Petra Sörling has said she could see him playing. Meanwhile Wang Chuqin won the 2025 world title and the 2026 World Cup.

The field goes beyond China. Brazil's Hugo Calderano and Japan's Sora Matsushima have both reached major finals recently.

Ties combine doubles and singles matches, so every team needs both men and women who can win. The format first appeared at the 2023 Mixed Team World Cup in Chengdu.

China has won each Mixed Team World Cup so far, including 8-1 over Japan in 2025. Hall 3 should offer fast, team-driven matches on Monday morning.

TTE34.blurb:
Two spots in the first-ever mixed team gold medal match are at stake in this semifinal. The loser drops to Saturday's bronze match.

China is the benchmark here, with Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha ranked world No. 1 in mixed doubles at the end of 2025. In the 2025 semifinal, China beat Korea Republic 8-3, even after Korea adjusted its lineup.

With a race to 8 games, one early mixed doubles win can set the tone. In a close hall with fans near the tables, every rally gets a reaction.

TTE35.blurb:
The second mixed team semifinal decides who plays for gold on July 29. Mixed team is new to the Games, replacing separate men's and women's team events.

Each tie is a race to eight games, played in sets in this order: mixed doubles, women's singles, men's singles, men's doubles, women's doubles. Teams need depth across all five.

If recent form holds, Japan and Germany are projected contenders, since they met in the 2025 Mixed Team World Cup semifinals. Japan reached that final, then lost 8-1 to China.

Expect a loud evening in Hall 3, where team ties can swing quickly and the crowd sits close to the tables.

The first-ever bronze medal match in this event is a Saturday-afternoon sendoff for the two semifinal losers. A medal is still on the line, which usually makes these matches fiercely competitive.

History suggests familiar names. In Chengdu in 2025, Korea Republic and Germany were the semifinal losers, and France and Chinese Taipei won men's team bronze at the 2026 World Team Championships.

The hall's close seating makes a bronze match feel more intimate than a big arena. Expect emotional celebrations as the loser's disappointment turns into a medal chase.

TTE37.blurb:
The first mixed team gold medal match in the Games arrives on Saturday night. It closes a new event and is the last big showpiece of the table tennis program.

China enters as the projected favorite, having won every Mixed Team World Cup since 2023 and all five table tennis golds at Paris 2024. Whether Fan Zhendong, Ma Long or Chen Meng return is unclear after they left the world rankings.

Japan are the likeliest challenger on form, after losing the 2025 final 8-1 and both 2026 team finals. The hall's close seating should make every point loud.

VBV01.blurb:
The first morning of beach volleyball at the 2028 Games begins in Long Beach with three pool-play matches. Every tournament has to start somewhere, and this is where 24 men's and 24 women's teams begin chasing the Round of 16.

The field is still taking shape, and pool draws have not been announced. Canada's Melissa Humana-Paredes and Brandie Wilkerson, Paris 2024 silver medalists, and the USA's Trevor Crabb and Chase Budinger have already won 2026 NORCECA titles that earned quota places for their countries.

Alamitos Beach Stadium puts temporary stands on open sand with the Pacific behind the court. A morning start suits fans who want an easy first taste of the sport in the place where it began.

Four pool-play matches fill the afternoon at Alamitos Beach, when the sun is high and the sand is hot. Pool results decide who reaches the single-elimination Round of 16, so even early matches carry weight.

If Sweden's David Ahman and Jonatan Hellvig are back, they arrive as Paris 2024 gold medalists and 2025 world champions. They also won the 2026 Joao Pessoa and Ostrava Elite events, though no 2028 roster is confirmed.

Expect a relaxed, sunny crowd, the sound of the surf behind the stands and a short walk to downtown Long Beach between matches.

Night beach volleyball arrives with three prelim matches under the lights. The late finish makes this a good fit for fans who want an after-dinner session.

Brazil's Ana Patricia and Duda won the Paris 2024 women's final 26-24, 12-21, 15-10, the first three-set women's final in Games history. Duda announced a break until November 2026, so whether the pair is intact for 2028 is an open question.

The temporary stadium glows against the dark Pacific, and the evening crowd tends to get loud as the night goes on.

The USA has already secured two men's quota places, with Trevor Crabb and Chase Budinger winning the 2026 NORCECA title. The second women's place is still undecided, and no U.S. teams have been officially named.

Arrive early to find a seat and take in the long, wide beach before the first serve. Morning light off the water makes this one of the prettier settings in the sport.

The afternoon crowd is relaxed and mixed, with fans in sunglasses and flags from all over. Late matches can see the sun drop toward the ocean.

The Peacock Theater puts every seat in front of one raised platform, so a lifter's walk-out and every chalked-hand clap is in clear view. The session runs about two hours in the evening, in air-conditioning, steps from L.A. Live.

The 2026 world title came down to a single kilogram. China's Zhang Haiqin totaled 221kg, just ahead of American Miranda Ulrey on 220kg, which hints at a tight night.

It is a late session, starting at 8:50 PM, in an indoor theater built for stage shows. Expect a hushed room as each lifter prepares and a roar when the bar goes overhead.

A looming question is Indonesia's Rizki Juniansyah, the Paris 2024 73kg champion, who was under an IWF provisional suspension in fall 2026 and whose case was unresolved. His 2028 status is uncertain.

WRE10.blurb:
Friday evening is a freestyle-heavy night. Semifinals run at men's 74kg and 125kg and women's 68kg, with medals decided in men's 57kg and 86kg and women's 62kg.

Japan is the headline team here. Rei Higuchi and Sakura Motoki won Paris 2024 gold in classes that are decided tonight.

Two big American names could also draw home-crowd roars: Kyle Dake at 86kg and Spencer Lee at 57kg, both if they qualify. Expect a late night at Hall 2.

WRE11.blurb:
Saturday morning covers men's freestyle 65kg and 97kg and women's 76kg. These are round-of-16 and quarterfinal bouts, with repechages for classes that have medals later that day.

The 97kg class carries real star power. Kyle Snyder won the 2025 world title, while Bahrain's Akhmed Tazhudinov won Paris 2024 gold, and reports on the 2026 final conflict.

Women's 76kg also has Paris history: Japan's Yuka Kagami beat the USA's Kennedy Blades in the final. This is a good early look at three loaded brackets in Hall 2.

WRE12.blurb:
Saturday night delivers a stacked card. Gold and bronze are on the line at men's freestyle 74kg and 125kg and women's 68kg, while semifinals run at 65kg, 97kg and women's 76kg.

The 125kg class is one to watch. Iran's Amir Hossein Zare won world titles in 2025 and 2026 and was Paris 2024 silver medalist. Gable Steveson is a wild card, saying he wants gold but that UFC is his priority.

Women's 68kg is the home-crowd draw if Amit Elor returns. Even so, this is a long, loud night at Hall 2.

WRE13.blurb:
Sunday afternoon closes out the wrestling program. Repechages, both bronze-medal matches and the gold-medal finals run in men's freestyle 65kg and 97kg and women's 76kg.

Three classes with real storylines end here. The 97kg class pairs Kyle Snyder with Bahrain's Akhmed Tazhudinov, if both qualify, and women's 76kg features Paris 2024 champion Yuka Kagami.

Because each class awards two bronze medals, fans see medals decided in quick succession. Expect a loud finale in Hall 2, the final session at the downtown venue.
